55:37.claim: The Quran anticipates modern astronomical photography of interstellar nebulae (such as the Cat's Eye Nebula or Rosette Nebula) by stating in Quran 55:37 that the sky will split open and become 'rose-colored like oil or paint' (fa-idhā inshaqqati al-samāʾu fa-kānat wardatan ka-l-dihān).
55:37.classification_explanation: Modern concordist commentators isolate [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) from its explicit eschatological context—the structural rupturing and physical liquefaction of the terrestrial sky dome on the Day of Resurrection ([Quran 55:35](quran://55/35)–[Quran 55:44](quran://55/44); [Quran 70:8](quran://70/8); [Quran 84:1](quran://84/1))—and project anachronistic meanings onto classical Arabic vocabulary (*wardah ka-l-dihān*). Concordist literature conflates two distinct classes of deep-space objects: planetary nebulae (such as the Cat's Eye Nebula, NGC 6543, an isolated dying star ~3,300 light-years away in Draco, ~0.4 light-years wide) and H II star-forming emission nebulae (such as the Rosette Nebula, NGC 2237, a giant molecular cloud ~5,200 light-years away in Monoceros, ~130 light-years wide, ionized by young O/B stars). Syntactically, the temporal conditional construction `fa-idhā ... fa-yawmaʾidhin` links the sky's rupture in [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) directly to the bodily interrogation and judgment of humans and jinn on the Day of Resurrection ([Quran 55:39](quran://55/39)–[Quran 55:43](quran://55/43)). The verse employs established Late Antique Near Eastern motifs of the solid celestial canopy melting like boiling oil dregs or dyed hide under divine judgment, as documented across classical Islamic exegesis ([Tafsir al-Tabari 55:37](tabari://55/37), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:37](ibnkathir://55/37)).
55:37.summary: In classical Arabic grammar and early commentaries (al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir), Quran 55:37 describes the Day of Judgment when the sky overhead splits open and melts like boiling oil dregs or red leather (*wardatan ka-l-dihān*) as humanity is judged (verses 39–43). By contrast, the Cat's Eye and Rosette Nebulae are ultra-thin vacuum clouds thousands of light-years away that look like faint grayish-green smudges to the human eye. Their vivid rose colors in NASA photos come from false-color filter mapping, and their petal-like rings are a viewing-angle projection of a hollow hourglass cylinder. Rather than describing modern astrophotography, the verse reflects pre-Islamic Biblical and Syriac apocalyptic traditions (like 2 Peter 3:10–12 and Jacob of Serugh) of the sky splitting and melting like hot oil on the Last Day.
55:37.refutation:
Philological, astrophysical, and historical evidence indicates that [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) does not describe or anticipate modern astronomical photography of interstellar nebulae. Rather than referring to deep-space objects imaged through orbital telescopes, the passage forms the climax of an eschatological pericope describing the structural dissolution and thermal liquefaction of the terrestrial sky dome on the Day of Resurrection. Classical Arabic lexicons, canonical early Islamic commentaries ([Tafsir al-Tabari 55:37](tabari://55/37), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:37](ibnkathir://55/37)), and contemporary Late Antique apocalyptic literature demonstrate that the phrase *wardatan ka-l-dihān* reflects an established Near Eastern motif: the solid celestial vault cracking open and melting into molten oil or red hide under divine fire.

---

### 1. Context of the Claim & Classical Arabic Philology (Wardah ka-l-Dihān)

Following warnings to humans and jinn regarding fire and smoke ([Quran 55:33](quran://55/33)–[Quran 55:36](quran://55/36)), [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) describes the cosmic scene:

> *"And when the heaven is split open and becomes rose-colored like murky oil [or red leather] –"* (`fa-idhā inshaqqati al-samāʾu fa-kānat wardatan ka-l-dihān`)

In the late 20th and early 21st centuries, concordist writers (such as Harun Yahya and Zaghloul El-Naggar) circulated visual comparisons pairing this verse with the AD 1994 NASA Hubble Space Telescope image of the **Cat's Eye Nebula (NGC 6543)** in Draco or the **Rosette Nebula (NGC 2237)** in Monoceros. Proponents proposed that the Arabic phrase *wardatan ka-l-dihān* anticipated the visual appearance of nebulae photographed through modern telescopes, interpreting the verse as a description of a celestial cloud resembling a red flower or paint in space.

#### Syntactic Protasis and Apodosis: The Eschatological Temporal Structure
From a grammatical and literary perspective, [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) is embedded within a continuous narrative sequence. In Arabic syntax, verse 37 begins with the temporal conditional particle *fa-idhā* (فَإِذَا, "and when"), forming a conditional protasis (*sharṭ*):
* **[Quran 55:37](quran://55/37)** (*protasis*): *"And when the heaven is split open and becomes rose-colored like murky oil..."*
* **[Quran 55:38](quran://55/38)** (*refrain*): *"Which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?"*
* **[Quran 55:39](quran://55/39)** (*apodosis*): *"Then on that Day neither human nor jinn will be questioned about his sin"* (`fa-yawmaʾidhin lā yusʾalu ʿan dhanbihi insun wa-lā jānn`).
* **[Quran 55:41](quran://55/41)–[Quran 55:43](quran://55/43)** (*continuation*): The angels seize the guilty by their forelocks and feet and cast them into Hellfire (*"This is the Hell which the criminals denied"*).

The syntactic construction `fa-idhā ... fa-yawmaʾidhin` grammatically and temporally links the sky's splitting (*inshaqqati al-samāʾ*) directly to the specific day (*yawmaʾidhin*) of bodily resurrection and judgment. Syntactically, the clause cannot be detached from the Day of Judgment to refer to deep-space nebulae that formed millennia ago while terrestrial history continues.

#### Classical Arabic Lexicography
Classical Arabic lexicography—documented in *Kitāb al-ʿAyn* by al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad (d. AD 786), *al-Ṣiḥāḥ* by al-Jawharī (d. AD 1003), *Lisān al-ʿArab* by Ibn Manẓūr (d. AD 1312), and Edward William Lane's *Arabic-English Lexicon* (bk. 1, p. 1435)—establishes the physical and contextual semantics of the vocabulary in [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37):

1. **Al-Samāʾ (السماء):** In classical Arabic and Quranic cosmology, *al-samāʾ* denotes the single, solid celestial canopy or vault arched directly above the Earth. It is governed here by the singular feminine verb *inshaqqat* (انشقت, "is cleaved, cracked open, or ruptured"), an eschatological verb denoting structural fracture. Across parallel Quranic descriptions of the Last Day, *inshaqqat* describes the physical rupturing of the terrestrial ceiling ([Quran 69:16](quran://69/16); [Quran 82:1](quran://82/1); [Quran 84:1](quran://84/1)), rather than the diffuse expansion of gas shells thousands of light-years away in interstellar space.
2. **Wardah (وردة):** While modern colloquial Arabic uses *wardah* for a garden rose, classical Arabic lexicographers and early exegetes emphasize its primary equine and chromatic meaning: a bay horse (*faras ward*, plural *wirād*). A bay horse is noted in classical Arabic poetry for possessing a coat that shifts hue according to seasonal temperatures—appearing yellow in the mild spring, turning deep red in winter, and darkening to a dusty hue under severe cold (*al-faras al-ward yakūnu fī al-rabīʿ aṣfar wa-fī al-shitāʾ aḥmar*). Chromatically, *wardah* denotes an intense, shifting reddish coloration (*lawn al-ward*), describing a sky that transitions from its customary blue or green to a shifting reddish-yellow hue under intense thermal stress.
3. **Al-Dihān (الدهان):** Classical Arabic lexicons record two primary meanings for *al-dihān*:
   * **Red-Tanned Leather or Hide (*al-adīm al-aḥmar*):** As recorded by al-Khalīl, al-Jawharī, and Ibn Manẓūr, *al-dihān* refers to animal hide saturated with red dye and oil during tanning until it turns smooth, glistening, and crimson.
   * **Boiling Oil Dregs or Melted Grease (*durdīy al-zayt / ʿakar al-zayt*):** Alternatively, *al-dihān* is the plural of *duhn* (oil, fat, or grease), denoting the sediment of oil that separates, bubbles, and glistens with shifting colors when heated over a furnace.

Rather than describing a botanical blossom or deep-space gas cloud, the phrase *wardatan ka-l-dihān* signifies that the solid ceiling of the sky will crack open and either turn deep red like oil-tanned leather or melt into glistening, boiling oil dregs under the heat of the Day of Judgment.

### 2. Astrophysical & Optical Empirical Analysis & Comparison Table

Concordist interpretations conflate two distinct classes of astronomical phenomena:
1. **Planetary Nebulae (such as NGC 6543, the Cat's Eye Nebula):** An expanding shell of ionized gas ejected by a single dying intermediate-mass star (~1 solar mass) transitioning into a white dwarf, located ~3,300 light-years away in Draco, spanning only ~0.4 light-years in diameter.
2. **H II Star-Forming Emission Nebulae (such as NGC 2237, the Rosette Nebula):** A vast, turbulent giant molecular cloud located ~5,200 light-years away in Monoceros, spanning ~130 light-years across, where thousands of new stars are currently coalescing and ionizing hydrogen gas through intense ultraviolet radiation from the central young open cluster NGC 2244.

Neither object corresponds to the physical narrative of [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) under optical, physical, or morphological analysis:

#### Narrowband False-Color Mapping vs. Human Vision (Scotopic vs. Photopic)
Concordist literature cites the vivid red, rose, and emerald hues of astrophotographs as representations of the visible sky. This correlation is inconsistent with optical physics and human retinal physiology:
* **The Scotopic Threshold of Human Vision:** The human eye possesses two primary photoreceptor systems: cone cells (responsible for photopic, color vision) and rod cells (responsible for scotopic, low-light monochromatic vision). Both NGC 6543 and NGC 2237 possess exceptionally low surface brightness. When viewed through human eyes—even with large optical telescopes—the light intensity is orders of magnitude below the threshold needed to trigger cone cells. Consequently, human vision operates exclusively in scotopic mode, where rod cells peak in sensitivity near green wavelengths (507 nm). To human observers looking through a telescope eyepiece, both nebulae appear as faint, ghostly, grayish-green or washed-out smudges. The brilliant crimson colors visible in photographs require hours of sensor integration and digital histogram stretching.
* **Artificial Narrowband Channel Assignments:** In the AD 1994 Hubble image of NGC 6543 taken by J. P. Harrington and K. J. Borkowski using WFPC2, the color palette is synthetic. Astronomers utilized narrowband interference filters to isolate specific atomic spectral lines: singly ionized nitrogen (`[N II]` at 658.4 nm), neutral hydrogen (`Hα` Balmer line at 656.3 nm), and doubly ionized oxygen (`[O III]` at 500.7 nm). Because `[N II]` (658.4 nm) and `Hα` (656.3 nm) are both physically crimson-red (separated by only 2.1 nm), displaying them in true visible color blurs their structural boundaries together. To separate the gas shells, NASA processors assigned `[N II]` to **red**, `Hα` to **green**, and `[O III]` to **blue**. Specifically, the hydrogen-alpha emission—which physically emits deep red light—was rendered **green**. Similarly, multi-hued images of the Rosette Nebula (NGC 2237) employ the Hubble SHO palette (`[S II]` mapped to red, `Hα` to green, `[O III]` to blue). The multi-colored "painted rose" appearance (*ka-l-dihān*) cited in concordist literature is a product of false-color channel assignments.

#### Physical Composition: Ultra-Rarified Vacuum Plasma vs. Viscous Liquefaction
Astrophysically, nebulae are ultra-tenuous interstellar vacuum plasmas with particle densities between $10^2$ and $10^4\text{ particles/cm}^3$. In comparison, sea-level air on Earth contains approximately $2.5 \times 10^{19}\text{ molecules/cm}^3$. The gas within NGC 6543 and NGC 2237 is more than a quadrillion times less dense than terrestrial air—a vacuum far more rarified than laboratory vacuums produced on Earth. Nebular plasma possesses zero viscosity, surface tension, or boiling fluid dynamics. Equating such rarified plasmas with boiling oil dregs (*ka-l-dihān*) or molten copper/oil ([Quran 70:8](quran://70/8) *ka-l-muhl*) is inconsistent with physical fluid dynamics.

#### Line-of-Sight Pareidolia
The perceived resemblance of NGC 6543 to a rose is a projection resulting from Earth's specific line-of-sight viewing angle. Three-dimensional kinematic modeling (Miranda & Solf, AD 1992; Reed et al., AD 1999) demonstrates that NGC 6543 is structurally a bipolar, nested hourglass-shaped cylinder with high-velocity polar jets ($v \approx 1,000\text{ km/s}$) and precessing collimated outflows. When viewed along its polar axis from Earth, the overlapping elliptical shells project the appearance of concentric flower petals. From an oblique perspective in space, the object appears as an asymmetric elongated hourglass lacking petal-like symmetry.

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr)

Classical commentators consistently interpreted [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) as an eschatological description of the physical destruction, color transformation, and thermal liquefaction of the celestial vault on the Day of Resurrection. In both [Tafsir al-Tabari 55:37](tabari://55/37) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:37](ibnkathir://55/37), the verse is explained through early exegetical authorities:

* **Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī:** Al-Ṭabarī (d. AD 923) defines the verse's eschatological setting:
  > *"He, Exalted is His remembrance, says: When the sky is split open and cleft asunder, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, its color will become the color of the red, rosy packhorse (*al-bardhawn al-ward al-aḥmar*)."*
  
  Al-Ṭabarī documents multiple transmissions from the Companions and Successors:
  * **Ibn ʿAbbās:** Transmitted through Qābūs from his father: *"Like the rosy horse (*ka-l-faras al-ward*).*" Through another chain (Ibn Saʿd): *"Its color changes."*
  * **Abū Ṣāliḥ & Mujāhid:** Abū Ṣāliḥ explained: *"Like the color of the rosy packhorse, then afterwards it becomes like oil."* Mujāhid stated: *"Like oil (*ka-l-duhn*).*"
  * **Al-Ḍaḥḥāk & Qatādah:** Al-Ḍaḥḥāk noted: *"The sky changes, and its color becomes like the color of the rosy animal."* Qatādah stated: *"Today it is green as you see, and its color on the Day of Resurrection will be a different color... its color on that Day will be redness (*al-ḥumrah*).*"
  * **Ibn Zayd:** Explained *wardatan ka-l-dihān* as: *"Radiant like oil (*mushriqatan ka-l-dihān*).*"
  * **Linguistic Meaning of Ka-l-Dihān:** Al-Ṭabarī notes that scholars differed between two explanations: some interpreted *dihān* as the plural of *duhn* (oil, in the radiance and glistening of its color), while others said it meant *al-adīm* (red-dyed leather). Al-Ṭabarī concludes: *"The most correct of the two sayings regarding that is the saying of the one who says: It means oil in the radiance of its color, because that is what is well-known in the speech of the Arabs."* (Note that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī does not appear in al-Ṭabarī's commentary on 55:37).

* **Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr:** Ibn Kathīr (d. AD 1373) states in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 55:37](ibnkathir://55/37) that the verse describes the physical melting and chromatic shift of the celestial sphere under eschatological heat:
  > *"[And it becomes Wardah like Dihan:] This means it will melt just as sediment and silver are melted when heated (*tadhūbu kamā yadhūbu al-durdīy wa-l-fiḍḍah fī al-sabk*). And it will be colored, just as dyes stain something, sometimes red, sometimes yellow, or blue, or green. This demonstrates the extent of the terrifying severity of the Mighty Day of Resurrection."*
  
  Ibn Kathīr attributes each early narration:
  * **Ibn ʿAbbās (via al-Ḍaḥḥāk):** *"It is red leather (`huwa al-adīm al-aḥmar`)."*
  * **Al-Baghawī:** Explains the equine metaphor: *"A rosy horse is yellow in the spring, red in the winter, and when the cold is severe, its color becomes dusty."*
  * **Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī:** Stated regarding the changing sky: *"It will be of different colors (`takūnu alwānan`)."*
  * **Qatādah:** Clarified: *"Today it is green, but on that Day its color will turn to red; a Day of different colors (`hiya al-yawma khaḍrāʾ wa-yawmaʾidhin lawnuhā ilā al-ḥumrah yawmu dhī alwān`)."*
  * **Mujāhid:** Interpreted *ka-l-dihān* as: *"Like the colors of dyes (`ka-alwān al-dihān`)."*
  * **ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī & Abū al-Jawzāʾ:** ʿAṭāʾ stated: *"Like the color of rose oil in its yellowness (`ka-lawni duhni al-wardi fī al-ṣufrah`)."* Abū al-Jawzāʾ explained: *"In the clarity of oil (`fī ṣafāʾi al-duhn`)."*
  * **Al-Suddī:** Explaining the physical liquefaction: *"It will be the color of a rosy mule, and it will be like molten copper/dregs (`ka-l-muhl`), like the sediment of oil (`ka-durdīy al-zayt`)."*
  * **[Abū Ṣāliḥ] Ibn Jurayj:** Stated: *"The sky will become like melted oil, and that is when the heat of Hellfire reaches it (*taṣīru al-samāʾu ka-l-duhn al-dhāʾib wa-dhālika ḥīna yuṣībuhā ḥarru jahannam*).*"

* **Parallel Quranic Verses:** Early exegetes cross-reference [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) with parallel passages depicting the structural dissolution of the heavens:
  * **[Quran 70:8](quran://70/8):** *"On the Day that the sky will be like molten metal [or boiling oil dregs] (`yawma takūnu al-samāʾu ka-l-muhl`)."*
  * **[Quran 69:16](quran://69/16):** *"And the heaven will be rent asunder, for that Day it will be frail and torn up (`fa-hiya yawmaʾidhin wāhiyah`)."*
  * **[Quran 82:1](quran://82/1) & [Quran 84:1](quran://84/1):** *"When the sky is cleft asunder (`infaṭarat`)"* and *"When the sky is split open (`inshaqqat`)."*

In classical Islamic scholarship, [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) describes the physical liquefaction of the sky vault into boiling liquid dregs under the heat of Gehenna, rather than an observation of deep-space interstellar nebulae.

### 4. Verbatim Pre-Islamic Apocalyptic & Biblical Precedents

The motif of the solid heavens splitting apart, turning blood-red, and melting like oil, pitch, wax, or molten metal on the Day of Judgment is a well-attested theme of Late Antique Jewish, Christian, and Biblical eschatology centuries prior to the 7th century AD:

1. **New Testament Apocalyptic Epistles:**
   * **[2 Peter 3:10](bible://2pt/3/10):** *"But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a roar and the elements will be destroyed with intense heat, and the earth and its works will be burned up."*
   * **[2 Peter 3:12](bible://2pt/3/12):** *"...looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which **the heavens will be destroyed by burning, and the elements will melt (`tēketai`, from `tēkō`, to liquefy or melt) with intense heat!**"*
   * In [2 Peter 3:12](bible://2pt/3/12), the Greek term *tēketai* expresses the same physical concept of thermal liquefaction (*tadhūbu*) that al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr employ to explain *ka-l-dihān* in [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37).
2. **Old Testament Prophetic Literature:**
   * **[Isaiah 34:4](bible://is/34/4):** *"And all the host of heaven will wear away, and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll; all their hosts will also wither away as a leaf withers from the vine, or as one withers from the fig tree."* (c. 8th–6th century BC).
   * **[Joel 2:30](bible://jl/2/30)–[Joel 2:31](bible://jl/2/31):** *"I will display wonders in the sky and on the earth, blood, fire and columns of smoke. The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and awesome day of the Lord comes."*
   * **[Revelation 6:12](bible://re/6/12)–[Revelation 6:14](bible://re/6/14):** *"The sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became like blood; and the stars of the sky fell to the earth... The sky was split apart like a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island were moved out of their places."* (c. late 1st century AD).
3. **Syriac Apocalyptic Literature & Late Antique Homilies:**
   * In the Late Antique Syriac Christian literature circulating in the pre-Islamic Near East, homilists described the end of the world through parallel imagery of the sky melting like oil or boiling resin:
     * **Ephrem the Syrian (d. AD 373):** In his *Memre on the End of the World* and *Hymns on Faith*, Ephrem depicts the cosmic dissolution where the solid arches of heaven melt like wax and lead before the divine flame.
     * **Jacob of Serugh (d. AD 521):** In his metrical homilies on the Last Judgment, Jacob of Serugh portrays the celestial firmament dissolving and pouring down like hot oil (*meshḥā*) when divine judgment ignites creation.
     * **The Apocalypse of Peter (c. 2nd century AD, Ethiopic recension ch. 5):** Describes the cosmic finale where the heavens liquefy: *"The stars shall melt in surges of fire, and the heaven shall pass away... and the heaven shall turn to water [liquefaction] and the earth shall be burned."*
     * **The Sibylline Oracles (Book II, lines 206–213; c. 2nd–3rd century AD):** Depicts the firmament melting into a boiling torrent of brimstone and liquid dregs under cosmic fire.

The Quranic description of the heavens splitting and melting into oil dregs (*ka-l-dihān*) or molten metal (*ka-l-muhl*) represents a continuation of this shared Near Eastern eschatological vocabulary.

### 5. Scholarly Evaluation of Modern Harmonizations

Modern concordist literature proposes several secondary harmonizations to align [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) with contemporary astrophysics. Each of these proposals diverges from primary physical, linguistic, and textual evidence:

* **Syntactic Separation of Verses 37 and 39 (`fa-idhā ... fa-yawmaʾidhin`):**
  * *Proposed Harmonization:* Some commentators suggest that verse 37 describes a general astronomical phenomenon in space, whereas verse 39 transitions to a separate eschatological scene.
  * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* This separation is unsupported by Arabic syntax. Verse 37 begins with *fa-idhā* (the conditional particle of time), which requires a fulfilling main clause (*jawāb al-sharṭ*). Verses 37–38 introduce the condition (*"And when the heaven is split open..."*), and verse 39 immediately supplies the grammatical apodosis (*"Then on that Day [`fa-yawmaʾidhin`] neither human nor jinn will be questioned..."*), followed by sinners being seized by forelocks and feet into Hell ([Quran 55:41](quran://55/41)–[Quran 55:43](quran://55/43)). The sky's transformation is grammatically bound as the direct prelude to bodily judgment and cannot refer to deep-space nebulae that formed millennia ago while earthly life continues.
* **The Hydrogen-Alpha Spectral Emission Reading (`Hα` at 656.3 nm):**
  * *Proposed Harmonization:* Concordist writers note that hydrogen-alpha (`Hα`) radiation emits at 656.3 nm in the physical red spectrum, arguing that nebulae are naturally red even when false-color channels are applied.
  * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* This reading does not account for two optical factors. First, due to extremely low surface brightness, nebulae do not reach the photon flux threshold required to stimulate human retinal cone cells (photopic color vision); to human eyes through a telescope, both NGC 6543 and NGC 2237 appear as faint, grayish-green smudges under scotopic rod vision. Second, because `Hα` (656.3 nm) and `[N II]` (658.4 nm) are both red, rendering them in true color blurs their structural features into a uniform wash (and in NGC 6543, teal `[O III]` emission is brighter than `Hα`). The multi-hued "painted rose" petals (*ka-l-dihān*) featured in concordist publications result from NASA mapping `[N II]` to red and `Hα` to green in NGC 6543 (or applying the Hubble SHO palette in NGC 2237).
* **The Solar Evolution Hypothesis (The Sun Becoming a Planetary Nebula):**
  * *Proposed Harmonization:* Some writers suggest that [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37) describes the distant future of the solar system, when the Sun will exhaust its core hydrogen, expand into a red giant, and eventually expel a planetary nebula in approximately 5 billion years.
  * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* This hypothesis is inconsistent with both stellar astrophysics and the narrative framework of Surah 55. When the Sun enters the asymptotic giant branch phase in ~5 billion years, its radius will expand beyond 1 astronomical unit (AU), engulfing and vaporizing Mercury, Venus, and Earth prior to the planetary nebula phase. Furthermore, a planetary nebula is an extended shell visible as a glowing disk only from an external vantage point across interstellar distances; an observer at the center of the system would experience an ionizing stellar wind and a bare white dwarf core at temperatures exceeding $100,000\text{ K}$. Textually, [Quran 55:37](quran://55/37)–[Quran 55:43](quran://55/43) depicts resurrected humans and jinn standing on the Earth, witnessing the immediate splitting of their sky before being seized by their forelocks and feet and cast into Hell, rather than an uninhabited stellar ejection billions of years in the future.
* **The Botanical Rose Reinterpretation:**
  * *Proposed Harmonization:* Writers propose that the word *wardah* denotes a botanical rose blossom (*Rosa*), comparing the concentric rings of gas in the Cat's Eye Nebula to rose petals.
  * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* In classical Arabic, *wardah* when applied to non-botanical phenomena denotes chromatic hue rather than floral morphology. As documented in *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*, *al-Ṣiḥāḥ*, *Lisān al-ʿArab*, and classical commentaries, the term specifies a red or bay coloration (*al-faras al-ward*) that shifts like dyed hide (*al-adīm al-aḥmar*). The verse contains no mention of petals, leaves, stems, or botanical structure. Equating a 7th-century chromatic descriptor of an eschatological sky with the floral anatomy of a rose blossom represents an anachronistic lexical retrojection.
* **Equating Dihān with Synthetic Paint or Modern Digital Pigments:**
  * *Proposed Harmonization:* Some contemporary translations render *ka-l-dihān* as "like paint" or "like an ointment," linking the verse to the colorful appearance of astrophotography prints.
  * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* In 7th-century Arabic, *dihān* referred specifically to natural liquid oils, animal fats, or oil-tanned leather. Interpreting a description of liquid fat melting under thermal stress as an allusion to modern synthetic pigments or digital RGB color palettes separates the term from its historical linguistic usage. The parallel description in [Quran 70:8](quran://70/8) (*yawma takūnu al-samāʾu ka-l-muhl*, "the Day the sky will be like molten copper / boiling oil dregs") confirms that the physical property emphasized is thermal liquefaction rather than artistic pigmentation.

53:45.claim: In Quran 53:45-46 ('And that He creates the two mates—the male and the female—from a drop when it is emitted'), the Quran miraculously anticipates modern chromosomal sex determination, proving that the biological sex of an infant is determined exclusively by the male sperm rather than the female egg.
53:45.classification_explanation: Modern concordist writers isolate the phrase 'from a drop, when it is emitted' (min nuṭfatin idhā tumnā) in [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) and retroactively map 20th-century chromosomal genetics (XX and XY sex chromosomes discovered in AD 1905) onto the 7th-century Arabic text. This reading separates the passage from its classical exegetical context ([Tafsir al-Tabari 53:45](tabari://53/45), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:45](ibnkathir://53/45)), which interprets the verse as a theological demonstration of divine resurrection from a generic seed-drop, as well as from canonical Prophetic traditions ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a)) and ancient Greco-Roman medical models (Hippocrates, Galen, and the Babylonian Talmud) that attributed sex determination to post-ejaculatory fluid competition between maternal and paternal secretions.
53:45.summary: In its classical Arabic context (al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir), Quran 53:45–46 simply observes that both males and females grow from an emitted drop of fluid (*nutfah*) as a sign of God's power to raise the dead, not that sperm carries X and Y chromosomes. When early Muslims asked how a baby's sex is determined, canonical Hadith (Sahih Muslim 315a and 2645a) stated that a boy forms if the man's fluid prevails over the woman's fluid—or a girl if hers prevails—and that an angel assigns sex forty-two nights after conception. Because sex is actually fixed at fertilization and female secretions play no genetic role, this model differs from modern cytogenetics. Instead, as the primary sources below detail, it reflects the pre-Islamic Greek and Talmudic medical theories of Hippocrates and Galen.
53:45.refutation:
Textual, historical, and biological evidence does not support the interpretation that [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) anticipates modern chromosomal sex determination. In cytogenetics, biological sex is determined at fertilization when an X-bearing or Y-bearing sperm fertilizes an X-bearing ovum. In contrast, [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) reflects the ancient observation that human beings originate from ejaculated reproductive fluid (*nuṭfah*). Classical Islamic exegesis ([Tafsir al-Tabari 53:45](tabari://53/45), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:45](ibnkathir://53/45)) understood this passage as a theological demonstration of divine resurrection, while canonical Hadith ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a), [Sahih al-Bukhari 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329), [Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a)) articulate the pre-Islamic Hippocratic-Galenic model of fluid dominance (*ʿalā*) and post-conception sex assignment at forty or forty-two days.

---

### 1. Context of the Claim & Classical Arabic Philology

In [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46), the text states:

> *"and that He created pairs, the male and the female, from a drop, when it is emitted;"* (`wa-annahu khalaqa al-zawjayni al-dhakara wa-l-unthā min nuṭfatin idhā tumnā`)

Modern concordist writers propose that by stating God creates male and female from an emitted drop (*nuṭfah*), the Quran anticipated the discovery of sex chromosomes (Nettie Stevens and Edmund Beecher Wilson, AD 1905). Because female ova carry X chromosomes while male sperm carry either an X or a Y chromosome, proponents suggest that the Quran identified male semen as the determinant of biological sex.

However, classical Arabic philology and historical context indicate that this interpretation projects modern genetic concepts onto ancient phenomenological language:

1. **Philology of *Nuṭfah* and *Tumnā*:** In classical Arabic (*Lisān al-ʿArab*, *Lane's Lexicon*, p. 2806), *nuṭfah* denotes a small drop of fluid, specifically semen. The verb *tumnā* (passive of *amnā*, root *m-n-y*) signifies emitting seminal fluid. Prior to the microscopic observation of spermatozoa (Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, AD 1677) and the mammalian ovum (Karl Ernst von Baer, AD 1827), pre-modern observers had no knowledge of microscopic gametes; semen was viewed macroscopically as the physical generative seed from which the fetus developed in the womb.
2. **Material Origin of Humanity vs. Genetic Allocation:** The phrase *min nuṭfatin idhā tumnā* identifies the **material origin of both sexes**, rather than an asymmetrical genetic mechanism. The verse observes that both sexes develop from emitted seminal fluid, as reiterated in [Quran 75:37](quran://75/37)–[Quran 75:39](quran://75/39) (*"Was he not a drop of semen emitted? [`nuṭfatan min maniyyin yumnā`] ... and made from it the two sexes, the male and the female."*).
3. **Application of *Manī* to Both Sexes:** In classical Arabic and Prophetic tradition, *manī* (root *m-n-y*) was not restricted to male semen. In [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a), Muhammad explicitly termed the woman's reproductive fluid *maniyy al-marʾah* (`مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ`, *"the woman's semen [manī]"*: `فَعَلَا مَنِيُّ الرَّجُلِ مَنِيَّ الْمَرْأَةِ ... وَإِذَا عَلَا مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ مَنِيَّ الرَّجُلِ`), while [Sahih Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311) affirms that a woman experiences nocturnal sexual emission like a man and discharges thin, yellow reproductive fluid (*māʾ al-marʾah*). Similarly, in [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:46](tabari://53/46), al-Ṭabarī explicitly glosses *idhā tumnā* using the verb *amnā* (root *m-n-y*) for both sexes (*"He created that from a drop, when the man and the woman emit it"* [`خلق ذلك من نطفة إذا أمناه الرجل والمرأة`]). Thus, *tumnā* in [Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) refers to reproductive emission generally rather than a male-specific chromosomal determinant.

---

### 2. Empirical Genetic & Textual Analysis

A comparison of modern cytogenetics with the Quranic and canonical Hadith model illustrates fundamental physiological differences:

| Aspect of Biological Sex Determination | Modern Chromosomal Genetics (XX / XY) | Quranic & Canonical Hadith Model ([Quran 53:45](quran://53/45); Sahih Muslim 315a) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Primary Mechanism** | Determined at syngamy by sex chromosomes: an X-bearing or Y-bearing haploid sperm fuses with an X-bearing ovum. The *SRY* gene on the Y chromosome triggers testis development. | Attributed to post-coital mechanical interaction between macroscopic male white fluid and female yellow fluid: whichever fluid dominates (*ʿalā*) determines biological sex. |
| **Timing of Sex Determination** | Fixed instantaneously at fertilization (the moment of conception) upon fusion of gamete pronuclei. | Described as undetermined during early pregnancy until 40 or 42 nights post-conception, when an angel asks Allah: *"O Lord, male or female?"* ([Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a)). |
| **Role of Maternal Secretions** | Female vaginal lubrication and orgasmic fluids play no genetic role; the mother contributes nuclear chromosomes exclusively through the ovum. | The mother's emitted fluid (*māʾ al-marʾah*) is described as an active, competing seminal agent that produces a female child if it prevails over the male fluid ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a)). |
| **Microscopic vs. Macroscopic Model** | Governed by microscopic haploid cellular gametes containing 23 pairs of chromosomes, invisible to the naked human eye. | Conceived as visible, macroscopic bodily fluids (*nuṭfah*, *manī*) differing in color and viscosity (white and thick for men, yellow and thin for women). |

In cytogenetics, chromosomal sex is established at syngamy. Females possess 46,XX chromosomes and produce X-bearing ova; males possess 46,XY chromosomes and produce equal ratios of X-bearing and Y-bearing sperm. Fertilization by an X-sperm yields a 46,XX female zygote, while a Y-sperm yields a 46,XY male zygote. Testis development is triggered at 6–7 weeks by the *SRY* gene on the short arm of the Y chromosome (Yp11.2), activating *SOX9*; in its absence, *WNT4* and *DAX1* guide ovarian development.

Modern cytogenetics diverges from the concordist model on two primary empirical grounds:
1. **Instantaneous Syngamy vs. Delayed Assignment:** Chromosomal sex is fixed at fertilization, whereas canonical Hadith state that embryonic sex remains unassigned until an angel inquires forty or forty-two days later ([Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a)).
2. **Genetic Invariance vs. Fluid Competition:** Maternal vaginal secretions play no genetic role in sex determination, whereas canonical Hadith attribute a female child to the woman's fluid prevailing over the man's fluid ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a)).

---

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr) and Canonical Ḥadīth

Classical Islamic scholarship did not interpret [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) as describing chromosomal sex determination. In *Jāmiʿ al-Bayān*, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (d. AD 923) explains [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45) strictly in terms of reciprocal pairs in creation:

> *"And His statement: {and that He created pairs, the male and the female, * From Nutfah when it is emitted}, He, may His mention be exalted, says: And that He originated the creation of the two mates, the male and the female, and made them two mates, because the male is a mate to the female, and the female is a mate to him."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 53:45](tabari://53/45))

In [Tafsir al-Tabari 42:49](tabari://42/49), al-Ṭabarī notes that bestowing male or female offspring represents a sovereign divine decree. Similarly, Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr (d. AD 1373) in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:45](ibnkathir://53/45) connects this verse directly to the theological doctrine of bodily resurrection:

> *"Allah said, {And that He creates the pairs, male and female. From Nutfah when it is emitted.} as He said: {Does man think that he will be left neglected? Was he not a Nutfah? Then he became an 'Alaqah (something that clings); then (Allah) shaped and fashioned (him) in due proportion. And made of him two sexes, male and female. Is not He (Allah) able to give life to the dead?} (75:36-40)"* ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 53:45](ibnkathir://53/45); cf. [Quran 75:36](quran://75/36)–[Quran 75:40](quran://75/40), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 75:39](ibnkathir://75/39)).

When early Muslims inquired about how an infant becomes male or female, Muhammad articulated the standard physiological model of Late Antiquity across canonical hadith:

1. **The Hadith of Thawbān ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a)):**
   When a Jewish scholar asked how a child becomes male or female, Muhammad replied:
   > مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ أَبْيَضُ وَمَاءُ الْمَرْأَةِ أَصْفَرُ فَإِذَا اجْتَمَعَا فَعَلَا مَنِيُّ الرَّجُلِ مَنِيَّ الْمَرْأَةِ أَذْكَرَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَإِذَا عَلَا مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ مَنِيَّ الرَّجُلِ آنَثَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
   > *"The reproductive water of the man is white and the reproductive water of the woman is yellow. When they meet, if the man's semen prevails over the woman's semen (`ʿalā maniyyu al-rajuli maniyya al-marʾati`), they produce a male by Allah's permission (`adhkarā bi-idhni Allāh`). And if the woman's semen prevails over the man's semen (`ʿalā maniyyu al-marʾati maniyya al-rajuli`), they produce a female by Allah's permission (`ānathā bi-idhni Allāh`)."* ([Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a))
2. **The Hadiths of Umm Sulaym ([Sahih Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311)) and ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329)):**
   In the narration of Anas ibn Mālik from Umm Sulaym on female nocturnal emission, Muhammad stated: *"The water of the man is thick and white, and the water of the woman is thin and yellow; from whichever of the two prevails or precedes (`ʿalā aw sabaqa`), from it comes the resemblance"* ([Sahih Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311)). Similarly, in Anas ibn Mālik's narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām's questions to the Prophet, Muhammad stated that if the man's discharge precedes the woman's (`sabaqahā māʾuhu`), the child resembles the father, whereas if the woman's discharge precedes (`sabaqa māʾuhā`), the child resembles her ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329)).
3. **The Forty-Two Nights Tradition ([Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a); [Sahih al-Bukhari 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318)):**
   Ḥudhayfah ibn Usayd reported that the Prophet said: *"When forty-two nights have passed over the drop (`nuṭfah`), Allah sends an angel to it, who shapes it... Then he says: 'O Lord, is it male or female?' (`ay rabbi adhakaron am unthā`), and your Lord decrees whatever He wills..."* ([Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a); cf. [Sahih al-Bukhari 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318)). This indicates that early Islamic tradition viewed embryonic sex as unassigned for the first six weeks of gestation.

---

### 4. Pre-Islamic Greek, Syriac, and Talmudic Precedents

The concepts of competing reproductive fluids and delayed embryonic sex determination correspond closely to well-documented Greco-Roman and rabbinic medical traditions:

1. **Hippocrates (*De Genitura* §§ 6–7, c. 420 BC):**
   In the 5th century BC, the Hippocratic treatise *On Generation* formulated the two-seed dominance theory:
   > *"Both the man and the woman produce both male seed and female seed... If both partners emit stronger seed, a male is born; if weak seed, a female. But if one emits stronger and the other weaker, whichever prevails in quantity (`hokoteron d' an kratēsē tō plēthei`), that is what turns out."* (Hippocrates, *De Genitura* §§ 6–7; translated by I. M. Lonie, *The Hippocratic Treatises*, Walter de Gruyter, AD 1981, pp. 4–5).
   The correspondence between Hippocrates' *kratein* (prevailing) and the canonical hadith's *ʿalā* (prevailing) in [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) reflects this shared conceptual framework.
2. **Aristotle (*De Generatione Animalium* IV.1, 4th century BC) and Galen (*De Semine* II.5, 2nd century AD):**
   Aristotle taught that sex determination depends upon whether the male formative heat masters (*kratei*) the cooler female matter (*De Generatione Animalium* IV.1, 766a–b). Claudius Galen synthesized this in *De Semine* (Kühn IV.626–642), holding that both parents emit seed and that the dominance of warmer male seed or moister female seed dictates sex and resemblance. These treatises were widely translated into Syriac by physicians such as Sergius of Reshaina (d. AD 536), establishing the medical consensus of the pre-Islamic Near East.
3. **The Babylonian Talmud (*b. Niddah* 31a; *b. Berakhot* 60a, compiled c. AD 500):**
   Late Antique rabbinic traditions articulated a parallel fluid-precedence doctrine:
   > *"Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Ammi: If the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male; if the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female, as it is stated: 'If a woman conceives seed and bears a male child' ([Leviticus 12:2](bible://lv/12/2))."* (Babylonian Talmud, *Tractate Niddah* 31a).
   Furthermore, the Talmud specifies a 40-day window for embryonic sex determination: *"Within the first forty days, one may pray for the sex of the child; after forty days, it is a vain prayer, for its sex has already been fixed"* (*Tractate Berakhot* 60a). This 40-day window parallels the forty-two nights tradition in [Sahih Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a). Early Islamic embryological descriptions thus situate within the shared medical and rabbinic milieu of Late Antiquity.

---

### 5. Scholarly Evaluation of Modern Harmonizations

Modern concordist writers advance two primary arguments to align [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) with chromosomal genetics, neither of which is supported by primary textual or historical evidence:

1. **The Argument from *Tumnā* (Emission):**
   Concordist authors propose that because [Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) uses the passive feminine verb *tumnā* (*"when it is emitted"*), referring grammatically to the feminine noun *nuṭfah* (drop), this refers exclusively to male ejaculation, indicating that the male fluid alone determines sex.
   *Philological & Primary-Source Assessment:* This reading conflates the general material origin of humanity with the genetic mechanism of sex determination. In pre-modern biology, reproduction was observed macroscopically to stem from seminal ejaculation. When [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45)–[Quran 53:46](quran://53/46) and [Quran 75:37](quran://75/37)–[Quran 75:39](quran://75/39) describe the creation of male and female from an emitted drop, the text notes that human beings of both sexes develop from ejaculated fluid; it does not describe chromosomes or differential genetic inheritance. Furthermore, classical Arabic exegesis and canonical hadith explicitly applied the root *m-n-y* to female reproductive fluid—terming it *maniyy al-marʾah* in [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) and glossing *idhā tumnā* as emission by both the man and the woman (*idhā amnāhu al-rajulu wa-l-marʾah*) in [Tafsir al-Tabari 53:46](tabari://53/46) (cf. [Sahih Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311) on female nocturnal emission and yellow reproductive fluid, *māʾ al-marʾah*).
2. **The Alternative Reading that *ʿAlā* Governs Resemblance Rather than Sex:**
   Some modern writers propose a secondary harmonization of [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) by suggesting that *ʿalā* (*"prevails"*) refers only to facial resemblance (*shabah*), assimilating it to [Sahih al-Bukhari 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329).
   *Textual & Primary-Source Assessment:* The Arabic text of [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) explicitly specifies biological sex using causative verbal conjugations:
   > فَعَلَا مَنِيُّ الرَّجُلِ مَنِيَّ الْمَرْأَةِ أَذْكَرَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَإِذَا عَلَا مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ مَنِيَّ الرَّجُلِ آنَثَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
   > *"...if the semen of the man prevails over the semen of the woman, they produce a male by Allah's permission (`adhkarā bi-idhni Allāh`); and if the semen of the woman prevails over the semen of the man, they produce a female by Allah's permission (`ānathā bi-idhni Allāh`)."*
   The verbs *adhkarā* (أَذْكَرَا, form IV dual: *"they two produce a male child"*) and *ānathā* (آنَثَا, form IV dual: *"they two produce a female child"*) derive directly from *dhakar* (male) and *unthā* (female). Classical commentators such as Imam al-Nawawī (d. AD 1277) in his commentary on Sahih Muslim (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, Kitāb al-Ḥayḍ) recognized that this narration addresses biological sex (*al-dhukūrah wa-l-unūthah*). Consequently, the hypothesis that early Islamic texts anticipated modern chromosomal sex determination is inconsistent with [Sahih Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a), which attributes sex determination directly to the relative dominance of maternal and paternal fluids.

39:21.claim: In Quran 39:21 ('Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs [yanābīʿ] in the earth...?'), the Quran is claimed to have miraculously anticipated modern hydrology by discovering the water cycle—specifically that underground springs and subterranean aquifers originate from infiltrating rainwater—a discovery concordist writers claim was unknown in the ancient world until Bernard Palissy in AD 1580.
39:21.classification_explanation: Modern concordist writers (originating with Maurice Bucaille in AD 1976 and popularized by Zakir Naik) isolate the phrase *anzala mina al-samāʾi māʾan fa-salakahu yanābīʿa fī al-arḍ* in [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21) and assert that the Quran was the first text in human history to describe the infiltration of rainwater into subterranean springs, claiming that ancient humanity prior to Bernard Palissy (AD 1580) universally believed springs originated exclusively from subterranean ocean abysses. This claim dehistoricizes [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21) from classical Arabic philology (where *a-lam tara* appeals to everyday naked-eye visual observation of seasonal desert flash floods replenishing local wells and springs), classical Islamic exegesis ([Tafsir al-Tabari 39:21](tabari://39/21) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:21](ibnkathir://39/21)), centuries of pre-Islamic Near Eastern hydraulic engineering (Nabataean water harvesting and Arabian *qanāt*/*falaj* aquifer galleries), explicit Biblical descriptions of the complete hydrological cycle ([Job 36:27](bible://jb/36/27)–[Job 36:28](bible://jb/36/28), [Ecclesiastes 1:7](bible://ec/1/7), [Amos 9:6](bible://am/9/6)), and extensive Greco-Roman meteorological treatises (Vitruvius and Aristotle) written 600 to 950 years before the Quran that explicitly documented rainwater percolation into springs while formulating the essential upward phase—oceanic evaporation—that the Quran omits.
39:21.summary: In its Arabic and exegetical context (al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr), Quran 39:21 appeals to everyday visual observation (*a-lam tara*, "Have you not seen?"): seasonal rain sinks into the ground, feeds local springs, and grows crops that soon wither as a parable of human mortality. Scientifically, this does not describe the modern water cycle because the Quran omits the essential upward engine—solar evaporation from the oceans—depicting rain instead as a one-way descent from heavenly stores. Historically, rainwater infiltration into springs was not unknown until AD 1580; Aristotle (c. 340 BC) and Vitruvius (c. 25 BC) documented rain filtering into mountain springs centuries before Islam, and Hebrew Scripture (Job 36:27–28, Ecclesiastes 1:7) already described both evaporation and the circular return of rivers to the sea.
39:21.refutation:
Assertions that [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21) anticipated modern hydrology by discovering the global water cycle or the infiltration of rainwater into subterranean springs are not supported by philological, historical, exegetical, and hydrogeological examination. In [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21), the text appeals to an everyday, naked-eye visual observation (*a-lam tara*) familiar to ancient agrarian and desert societies: seasonal rainfall enters the ground and emerges as springs, sustaining crops that eventually wither and dry up as an emblem of human mortality. Crucially, the Quran omits the fundamental, unobservable mechanism that transforms water flow into a closed *cycle*—namely, solar evaporation of water vapor from the oceans into the atmosphere. Furthermore, the infiltration of rainwater through rock strata into subterranean springs was explicitly documented more than six to nine centuries before the Quran by Greco-Roman naturalists such as Aristotle (c. 340 BC) and Vitruvius (c. 25 BC), while Hebrew Scripture ([Job 36:27](bible://jb/36/27)–[Job 36:28](bible://jb/36/28), [Ecclesiastes 1:7](bible://ec/1/7), [Amos 9:6](bible://am/9/6)) articulated the circular return of water to the sea and its upward distillation from the deep over a millennium prior to Islam.

---

### 1. Context of Claim & Classical Arabic Philology

In the late 20th century, concordist author Maurice Bucaille (*The Bible, The Qur'an and Science*, AD 1976) and subsequent commentators such as Zakir Naik asserted that [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21)—alongside [Quran 23:18](quran://23/18) and [Quran 15:22](quran://15/22)—represents an advanced scientific insight. Bucaille proposed that human understanding of hydrology remained inaccurate until the French ceramicist and natural philosopher Bernard Palissy published his discourse on waters and springs in AD 1580. According to Bucaille, ancient natural philosophy, following Plato, maintained that springs were fed exclusively by subterranean ocean abysses pushing water upward through pressure, making the Quran the first text in human history to state that springs (*yanābīʿ*) originate from rainwater percolating into the soil (*anzala mina al-samāʾi māʾan fa-salakahu yanābīʿa fī al-arḍ*).

Philological analysis of classical Arabic lexicography and rhetoric demonstrates that this concordist reading diverges from the linguistic and historical context of the verse:

* **The Visual Marker `A-lam tara` (`أَلَمْ تَرَ` — "Have you not seen...?" / "Do you not see...?"):**
  * In classical Arabic grammar and rhetorical exegesis (*balāghah*), the Form I jussive interrogative *a-lam tara* (from the root *r-ʾ-y*) functions as an appeal to ocular, naked-eye verification (`al-ruʾyah al-baṣariyyah`) or universally acknowledged empirical reality (`al-ʿilm al-yaqīnī al-mushāhad`). Across the Quran, *a-lam tara* regularly introduces visible natural phenomena accessible to any 7th-century observer (e.g., [Quran 22:63](quran://22/63), *"Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky and the earth becomes green?"*; [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43), *"Do you not see that Allah drives clouds?"*; [Quran 31:29](quran://31/29), *"Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day?"*; [Quran 105:1](quran://105/1)).
  * For 7th-century Arabian desert dwellers, transhumant pastoralists, and oasis farmers, the connection between seasonal downpours and the emergence of springs was an immediate visual reality. In the arid topography of the Hejaz and Najd, torrential seasonal rainstorms (*suyūl*) swept down dry riverbeds (*widyān*), ponded in alluvial plains, and visibly replenished natural rock basins, shallow wells (*ābār*), and mountain springs (*ʿuyūn* and *yanābīʿ*, singular *yanbūʿ*, from the root *n-b-ʿ*, meaning to well forth or gush). Observing a dry subterranean fissure or spring begin gushing water days or weeks after heavy mountain rains required no specialized instrumentation; it formed the practical basis of desert survival.
* **The Structural Absence of Oceanic Evaporation (The Missing Half of the Hydrological Cycle):**
  * Modern hydrology defines the hydrological cycle as a continuous closed-loop thermodynamic system. The primary driving engine of this cycle is **solar-driven evaporation from the surface of the oceans and seas**, lifting millions of cubic kilometers of water vapor into the troposphere to condense into precipitation.
  * If water merely falls from heaven, enters the earth, and flows out of springs without an upward oceanic return, it represents an open, one-way downward cascade—not a cycle.
  * Notably, nowhere in [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21), [Quran 23:18](quran://23/18), [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43), [Quran 30:48](quran://30/48), or anywhere across the 6,236 verses of the Quran, is oceanic evaporation described or implied. The Quran does not explain how water reaches the clouds from the sea.
  * Instead, the text operates within the ancient Near Eastern cosmology of a celestial dome above which water is held in heavenly storehouses ([Quran 15:21](quran://15/21), *"And there is not a thing but with Us are its stores, and We do not send it down except in a known measure"*; [Quran 23:18](quran://23/18), *"And We sent down from the sky water in measure, and We lodged it in the earth"*). Winds are depicted not as vapor evaporators from oceans, but as celestial drivers that herd pre-existing clouds ([Quran 30:48](quran://30/48)). The essential physical mechanism that makes hydrology a closed cycle is thus absent from the text.

In the historical record, however, Plato's literary account was immediately critiqued and revised by his own student Aristotle in *Meteorologica* (I.13). Greco-Roman naturalists recognized that rainfall and snowmelt infiltrate the soil and feed springs through rock fissures (*venae terrae*). Vitruvius in *De Architectura* (c. 25 BC) provided an extensive engineering manual detailing how rainwater gathers in underground mountain strata and flows out as perennial springs—sixteen centuries before Palissy and over six hundred years before the Quran.
2. **The Ancient Formulation of the Thermodynamic Water Cycle:** The cyclical nature of water—evaporation by solar heat, atmospheric cooling and cloud condensation, precipitation as rain, and return via rivers to the ocean—was thoroughly established in Mediterranean natural philosophy. Xenophanes of Colophon (6th century BC) stated that the sea is the source of all clouds, winds, and rivers (DK 21 B30). Anaxagoras (5th century BC) and Aristotle (*Meteorologica* I.9, 346b–347a) described the process as a continuous circle (*kyklos*). Vitruvius (*De Architectura* VIII.2.1–4) detailed how the sun draws up marine moisture to create rain clouds that strike mountain slopes, discharge their water, and filter into subterranean aquifers.
3. **Pre-Islamic Near Eastern Hydraulic Engineering:** Long before the 7th century AD, civilizations across the arid Near East and the Arabian Peninsula demonstrated advanced practical knowledge of groundwater hydrology:

Hegra, located in northwestern Saudi Arabia approximately 300 kilometers north of Medina, possessed over 130 rock-cut wells tapping the subterranean water table fed by seasonal infiltration.
   * **Arabian and Persian Qanāt / Falaj Systems (1st Millennium BC Onward):** Throughout Oman (*aflāj*), Yemen, and eastern Arabia, ancient engineers excavated gently sloping underground galleries (*qanāt* / *kārīz*) that tapped perched aquifers in alluvial fans at the foot of mountain ranges, conducting groundwater over tens of kilometers to surface oases. These systems demonstrate that ancient inhabitants understood that rainwater recharging mountain roots created subterranean water reserves.
   * **The Great Dam of Maʾrib (8th Century BC – AD 575):** In ancient Yemen, the Sabaeans constructed the Maʾrib Dam to capture seasonal flash floods from the Dhana valley, channeling millions of cubic meters of water to irrigate 25,000 acres of farmland. The hydrological relationship between seasonal rainfall and surface and subsurface water availability was foundational to Arabian agriculture and settlement for over a millennium before the compilation of the Quran.

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr)

Rather than reading a 20th-century thermodynamic hydrological cycle into [Quran 39:21](quran://39/21), classical Islamic exegetes understood the verse as an appeal to visible agrarian reality serving a theological purpose: illustrating God's power to resurrect dead bodies from the earth on the Day of Judgment.

#### Exegesis of Quran 39:21 in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī

In [Tafsir al-Tabari 39:21](tabari://39/21), Abu Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (d. AD 923) explains the passage strictly through naked-eye visual observation and classical lexicography:

> *"He whose remembrance is exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad: {Do you not see} O Muhammad {that God has sent down water from the sky}, which is the rain, {and put it into the earth as springs}. He says: So He made it flow as springs in the earth. The singular of it is yanbūʿ, and it is that which gushes forth from the earth...*
> 
> *Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from al-Shaʿbī, regarding His saying: {and put it into the earth as springs}, he said: 'Every dew and water in the earth has descended from the sky.'*
> 
> *He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim ibn Bayān, he said: Then He brings forth by means of that water which He sent down from the sky, and made it springs in the earth, crops {of various colors}, meaning: various kinds among wheat, barley, sesame, rice, and the like of various kinds... {and then they wither, and you see them turning yellow}... It is said of the earth when what is in it of greenness dries and withers: 'The earth has withered,' and 'The crops have withered.'... {and then He makes them broken debris}... And al-ḥuṭām is the crumbled fragments of straw and grass."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 39:21](tabari://39/21))

Crucially, al-Ṭabarī clarifies the theological intent of the entire passage:
> *"He whose remembrance is exalted says: Surely in Allah's doing of that, as He has described, is a reminder and an admonition for the people of intellect... Thus they know that the One who does that, it will never be impossible for Him to bring about whatever He wills... and to bring to life whoever perished from His creation after his death, and to restore him after his perishing, to his form before his perishing, just like that which He did to the earth upon which He sent down water after its death, thereby bringing forth crops of various colors by His power."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 39:21](tabari://39/21))

#### Exegesis of Quran 39:21 in Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr

In [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:21](ibnkathir://39/21), Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr (d. AD 1373) titles his chapter *"Water Originates in the Sky, and the Parable of the Life of This World"*, emphasizing the literal descent of all terrestrial water from the sky:

> *"Allah tells us that the origin of water in the earth is from the sky (`yukhbiru taʿālā anna aṣla al-māʾi fī al-arḍi min al-samāʾ`), as He says: {and We send down pure water from the sky} ([Quran 25:48](quran://25/48)). So when Allah sends down water from the sky, it settles in the earth, then He causes it to flow in the parts of the earth wherever He wills, and He causes springs, great and small, to flow as needed. This is why Allah says: {and put it into the earth as springs}.*
> 
> *Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, Abu Qutaybah ʿUtbah ibn Yaqẓān narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding Allah's saying: {Do you not see that God has sent down water from the sky, and put it into the earth as springs}, he said: 'There is no water in the earth except that it descended from the sky, but veins in the earth change it (`laysa fī al-arḍi māʾun illā nazala min al-samāʾi wa-lākinna ʿurūqan fī al-arḍi tughayyiruhu`), so that is Allah's saying: {and put it into the earth as springs}, so whoever is pleased that salty water returns to being sweet, let him vaporize it [distill it, `fa-lyuṣaʿʿidhu`].'*
> 
> *Likewise, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī said that all the water on earth has its origin in the sky. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Its origin lies in the snow, meaning that snow piles up on the mountains, then settles at their base, and springs flow from the bottom of them (`anna al-thalja yatarākamu ʿalā al-jibāli fa-yaskunu fī qarārihā fa-tanbaʿu al-ʿuyūnu min asāfilihā`)."* ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:21](ibnkathir://39/21))

Crucially, the final clause attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās (`fa-man sarrahu an yaʿūda al-milḥu ʿadhban fa-lyuṣaʿʿidhu` — *"so whoever is pleased that salty water returns to being sweet, let him vaporize/distill it"*) does not refer to natural solar evaporation from the oceans, nor does it appear in the Quranic text. Rather, *taṣʿīd* (`تَصْعِيد`) is the classical technical term for artificial human boiling and alembic distillation: Ibn ʿAbbās is offering an everyday empirical illustration that brackish well water was originally sweet rainwater descending from the sky that subsequently absorbed mineral salts from subterranean earth-veins (`ʿurūq fī al-arḍ`), since boiling salty groundwater and condensing its steam removes the dissolved salts—an experiment already documented nearly a millennium earlier by Aristotle (*Meteorologica* II.3, 358b) and Alexander of Aphrodisias.

Regarding the second half of the verse, Ibn Kathīr stresses the moral parable of worldly transience:
> *"{Surely in that is a reminder indeed to those with understanding} means, those who are reminded by this and who learn the lesson from it, that this world is like this: it is green, fresh, and beautiful, then it becomes old and ugly. The young man becomes a weak, senile old man, and after all of that comes death... Allah often likens the life of this world to the way He sends down water from the sky and crops grow thereby, then they become dry and brittle, as He says: {And put forward to them the example of the life of this world: it is like the water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and becomes fresh and green. But later it becomes dry and broken pieces, which the winds scatter} ([Quran 18:45](quran://18/45))."* ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 39:21](ibnkathir://39/21))

#### The Exegetical Understanding of Quran 23:18 and Extraterrestrial Water Stores

In [Quran 23:18](quran://23/18) (*"And We sent down from the sky water in measure, and We lodged it in the earth, and We are indeed able to take it away"*), classical authorities likewise explained terrestrial groundwater as a one-way vertical deposit from the sky rather than a closed oceanic evaporation loop. In [Tafsir al-Tabari 23:18](tabari://23/18), al-Ṭabarī glosses the verse as: *"And We sent down from the sky whatever water is in the earth, and We lodged it therein"* (`wa-anzalnā mina al-samāʾi mā fī al-arḍi min māʾin fa-askannāhu fīhā`), citing Ibn Jurayj's report that the water descended from the sky and settled in the earth. Similarly, in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 23:18](ibnkathir://23/18), Ibn Kathīr explains that God lodges the descending celestial water in the earth and threads it as springs (`fa-yuskinuhu fī al-arḍi wa-yaslukuhu yanābīʿa fī al-arḍi`). Later encyclopedic commentators—such as al-Qurṭubī in *al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān* and al-Suyūṭī in *al-Durr al-Manthūr* under [Quran 23:18](quran://23/18) (paralleling the canonical hadith in [Sahih Muslim 2839](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2839))—further preserved traditions that the great rivers of the earth (the Nile, the Euphrates, Saihan, and Jaihan) descend directly from celestial Paradise beneath the Divine Throne. Early Islamic scholarship thus understood these passages as a linear vertical descent where God releases measured stores of water from the heavenly vault into subterranean pockets.

### 4. Verbatim Pre-Islamic Classical, Biblical & Near Eastern Hydrological Texts

More than half a millennium to a millennium before the compilation of the Quran, Greek, Roman, and Hebrew authors recorded detailed descriptions of rainwater infiltration into springs and the complete circular hydrological cycle:

#### 1. Vitruvius (c. 25 BC): Infiltration into Springs and Atmospheric Evaporation

In his masterwork *De Architectura* (c. 25 BC), dedicated to the Roman Emperor Augustus, the Roman architect and military engineer Vitruvius Pollio detailed both the infiltration of rainwater into subterranean mountain springs and the complete cycle of solar evaporation:

* **Infiltration of Rain and Snow into Mountain Springs (*De Architectura*, Book VIII, Ch. 1, Sec. 6–7):**
  > *"Springs that rise in plains are salty, coarse, lukewarm, and unpleasant... But those that burst out in mountains or wooded hills are of the sweetest and healthiest water, because falling snow and rain, percolating through the hidden veins of the earth (`per venas terrae`), are cooled and filtered by the rocky depths until they emerge at the base of the mountains as flowing springs (`fontes`). For the moisture of rain and snow penetrates into the open cavities of the earth, and sinking down through the porous earth and rock strata, it collects upon impermeable layers of stone and clay, bursting forth wherever a channel finds an opening."*
* **The Full Evaporation and Precipitation Cycle (*De Architectura*, Book VIII, Ch. 2, Sec. 1–4):**
  > *"The sun's heat draws up moisture from the earth and from the sea... The air, being heated by the sun, expands and carries the vapor aloft into the upper atmosphere. There, driven by winds and striking against cold mountain ranges, the vapors condense into dense clouds and fall as rain. That water, penetrating into the earth, replenishes the veins of springs and feeds the continuous flow of rivers back into the sea."*

Vitruvius explicitly formulated both the infiltration model that Bucaille attributed to Palissy and the upward oceanic evaporation phase that does not appear in the Quran, more than six centuries before Islam.

#### 2. Aristotle (c. 340 BC): The Continuous Hydrological Circle

In his treatise *Meteorologica* (Book I), Aristotle (384–322 BC) formulated the principles of physical hydrology based on thermodynamics and observational mechanics:

* **The Thermodynamic Circle (*Meteorologica*, Book I, Ch. 9, 346b–347a):**
  > *"The sun, moving as it does, causes evaporation and heat... The moisture raised by heat is drawn up into the upper region; when the heat that raised it leaves it, the vapor cools and condenses again into water. Having become water, it falls back again to the earth. The evaporation of water is vapor; the condensation of air into water is cloud... Thus a circle is formed (`kyklos`), following the movement of the sun."*
* **Mountain Infiltration and Spring Formation (*Meteorologica*, Book I, Ch. 13, 349b–350a):**
  > *"The mountains act like an immense sponge hung up over the plains; they receive the rain that falls upon them, and the moisture gradually trickling down through many small cavities unites into larger streams, bursting forth as springs (`pēgai`) at their base... It is evident that water trickling together drop by drop into the earth collects in underground reservoirs, from which springs and rivers take their origin."*

#### 3. Lucretius (c. 55 BC) & Pliny the Elder (AD 77)

* **Lucretius (*De Rerum Natura*, Book VI, lines 608–638):** The Roman poet and philosopher Lucretius addressed why the ocean does not increase in size despite receiving all rivers:
  > *"First, the sun with its heat sucks up a vast amount of water; and the winds sweeping over the sea carry off much... Moreover, the earth is porous; as water filters down through the soil, it leaves its salt behind and flows back, pure and fresh, through subterranean veins to gather at the head of river springs, whence it runs once more down its sweet-water course."*
* **Pliny the Elder (*Naturalis Historia*, Book II, Ch. 65–66, AD 77):** Pliny described how moisture evaporated by the sun condenses into clouds, descends as rain, penetrates the soil, and re-emerges through subterranean fissures to feed rivers and lakes.
