### 1. Context of Claim & Classical Arabic Philology (Zawjayn and Kulli Shayʾ)

Following the rise of modern scientific concordism in the late 20th century—championed by popular writers such as Harun Yahya (*The Miracles of the Qur'an*, AD 2001), Zakir Naik, and widely disseminated dawah literature—proponents isolated the clause *wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayni laʿallakum tadhakkarūn* (*"And of all things We created two pairs, so that you may remember"*) in [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49), frequently cross-referencing [Quran 36:36](quran://36/36) (*"Glory be to Him Who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know"*).

Concordists put forward two principal interpretations of this verse:

1. **The Biological Claim:** Concordists argue that the verse states an universal biological law that all living organisms are created in male and female sexual pairs, a biological reality they contend was unknown in the 7th century AD.
2. **The Quantum Antimatter Claim:** In response to microbiological evidence demonstrating that numerous organisms reproduce asexually without distinct sexes, an alternative concordist reading appeals to subatomic physics. Proponents argue that *zawjayn* anticipates Paul Dirac's AD 1928 relativistic electron equation predicting the positron (experimentally confirmed by Carl Anderson in AD 1932), proposing that every particle in nature was described as possessing an antimatter counterpart.

A philological examination of classical Arabic lexicography and Quranic syntax indicates that neither modern reading aligns with the historical semantics of the text:

* **Classical Arabic Lexicography of *Zawj* (زوج) and *Zawjayn* (زوجين):** In authoritative classical lexicons—including *Kitāb al-ʿAyn* by al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad (d. AD 786), *al-Ṣiḥāḥ* by al-Jawharī (d. AD 1003), *Lisān al-ʿArab* by Ibn Manẓūr (d. AD 1312), and Edward William Lane's *Arabic-English Lexicon* (Book I, pp. 1262–1263)—the root *z-w-j* fundamentally signifies the pairing, coupling, or uniting of two things. A *zawj* is one of a pair, a counterpart, a companion, or an equivalent sort (*ṣinf* / *nawʿ*). In the dual form *zawjayn*, it denotes "two counterparts," "two sorts," or "a pair."
  In classical Arabic and Quranic usage, *zawj* operates within two distinct semantic registers:
  * **Biological Spouses / Sexual Mates (*al-dhakar wa-l-unthā*):** When the Quran specifically intends biological reproductive sexes, it explicitly appends the qualifying adjectives: *wa-annahū khalaqa al-zawjayni al-dhakara wa-l-unthā* (*"And that He created the two pairs, the male and the female"*, [Quran 53:45](quran://53/45); cf. [Quran 75:39](quran://75/39); [Quran 42:11](quran://42/11)). The presence of *al-dhakar wa-l-unthā* demonstrates that *zawjayn* alone does not inherently mean biological male and female.
  * **Correlative Categories, Kinds, or Polar Opposites (*ṣinf*, *nawʿ*, *lawn*):** In broad cosmological and ontological contexts, *zawj* signifies a distinct category, sort, or contrasting pole. Thus, the plural *azwāj* repeatedly means "kinds" or "classes": in [Quran 56:7](quran://56/7), humanity is divided on Judgment Day into *azwājan thalāthah* (*"three kinds"*); in [Quran 20:53](quran://20/53), the text refers to *azwājan min nabātin shattā* (*"diverse kinds of vegetation"*); and in [Quran 38:58](quran://38/58), it describes punishments of *ākharu min shaklihī azwāj* (*"others of similar kinds"*). Applied to macrocosmic phenomena, *zawjayn* denotes complementary polar opposites: sky and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, happiness and misery.
* **The Theological Context of Monotheism (*Tawḥīd*):** The concluding clause of [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) states *laʿallakum tadhakkarūn* (*"so that you may remember"*). In classical Islamic rhetoric and theology, the explicit purpose of observing duality in creation is to contrast creaturely contingency and multiplicity with the absolute, unpaired Oneness (*al-Wāḥid*, *al-Fard al-Ṣamad*) of the Creator. Created things are defined by duality, pairing, and dependence on a counterpart; only God exists as Singular and Indivisible, possessing neither counterpart (*nidd*), partner (*sharīk*), nor opposite.
* **The Syntax of *Kulli Shayʾ* (كل شيء) as *Al-ʿĀmm al-Makhṣūṣ*:** In classical Arabic grammar and Quranic hermeneutics (*uṣūl al-fiqh*), the universal quantifier *kull* ("every" / "all") frequently functions as *al-ʿāmm al-makhṣūṣ*—a general expression whose scope is contextually delimited to familiar macro-categories known to the human audience, rather than a mathematically absolute quantifier spanning unseen micro-particles or microscopic taxonomy. This is demonstrated by parallel Quranic usages:
  * In [Quran 46:25](quran://46/25), the destructive wind sent against ʿĀd is said to "destroy everything by the command of its Lord" (*tudammiru kulla shayʾin bi-amri rabbihā*), yet the text immediately notes: *fa-aṣbaḥū lā yurā illā masākinuhum* (*"so that nothing could be seen except their dwellings"*). The dwellings, the ground, and the atmosphere were manifestly not destroyed.
  * In [Quran 27:23](quran://27/23), the Queen of Sheba is described as having been given "of everything" (*wa-ūtiyat min kulli shayʾin*), which clearly did not encompass Solomon's kingdom, prophetic wisdom, or command over the jinn.
Within the linguistic framework of 7th-century Arabia, *wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn* conveyed that the observable realities of the cosmos are fashioned in complementary pairs, bearing witness to the unique singularity of their Creator.

### 2. Particle Physics & Biological Empirical Analysis

When concordists interpret [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) as a scientific statement describing universal physical or biological realities, their readings diverge from established empirical findings across microbiology, zoology, mycology, and quantum field theory:

| Scientific Domain | Modern Empirical Science | Concordist Claim vs. Classical Meaning of [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Prokaryotes & Unicellular Eukaryotes (Asexual Reproduction)** | Bacteria, Archaea, and protists (e.g., *Amoeba*, *Euglena*) reproduce strictly through binary fission, budding, or mitosis. They possess no biological sexes, male/female gametes, or sexual pairings. | Concordists claim all living organisms exist in male and female pairs. Empirically, the vast majority of life by individual count, species diversity, and evolutionary history is non-sexual. |
| **Obligate Parthenogenetic Animals (All-Female Species)** | Numerous metazoan species reproduce exclusively via obligate parthenogenesis without males, including bdelloid rotifers (over 40 million years without males), whiptail lizards (*Aspidoscelis neomexicanus*), and Brahminy blind snakes. | Diverges from the premise of universal sexual pairing. These species consist of 100% female populations that reproduce independently, lacking male mates (*zawj*) entirely. |
| **Fungal Mating Systems (Multiallelic Sexes)** | Many fungi do not possess two sexes; basidiomycetes such as *Schizophyllum commune* possess tetrapolar mating systems with over 23,000 distinct biological mating types (sexes). | Inconsistent with a strictly binary definition of *zawjayn* ("two pairs"). Fungal reproduction involves thousands of compatible mating types rather than a binary pair. |
| **Quantum Field Theory: Self-Conjugate Bosons** | In the Standard Model of Particle Physics, fundamental bosons mediating interactions—including the photon (γ), neutral Z boson (Z⁰), and Higgs boson (H⁰)—are strictly self-conjugate, acting as their own antiparticles. | Concordists claim every particle has a distinct antiparticle pair. Self-conjugate particles have no distinct antiparticle mate, diverging from the premise of universal particle duality. |
| **Cosmological Baryon Asymmetry** | The observable universe is overwhelmingly composed of matter, with approximately 10⁹ photons per baryon and virtually zero primordial antimatter due to early baryogenesis. | Inconsistent with the model of a symmetrically paired cosmos. The universe is characterized by pronounced matter-antimatter asymmetry rather than equal, balanced pairs. |

#### Detailed Biological Breakdown

1. **Prokaryotes (Bacteria and Archaea) Lack Sexual Pairs:** Prokaryotes represent the earliest, most abundant, and most metabolically diverse forms of life on Earth, encompassing trillions of species. Prokaryotes reproduce exclusively via **binary fission**—an asexual process in which a single parent cell replicates its circular DNA and divides into two identical daughter cells. There are no male or female cells, no sperm or egg gametes, and no sexual pairings. Mechanisms of horizontal gene transfer (conjugation, transformation, and transduction) are non-reproductive processes of lateral DNA exchange, not sexual reproduction or the union of sexual pairs.
2. **Viruses and Viroids Have No Sexes:** Viruses, viroids, and subviral satellites constitute a vast biological realm. They possess no cellular structure, perform no sexual reproduction, and are neither male nor female. They replicate purely by hijacking host cellular machinery.
3. **Asexual Unicellular Eukaryotes:** Countless single-celled eukaryotes—such as *Amoeba proteus*, *Euglena gracilis*, and numerous flagellates and ciliates—reproduce purely through asexual mitosis, longitudinal fission, or budding without any male or female dimorphism.
4. **Obligate Parthenogenetic Animals (All-Female Species):** Even among complex multicellular animals (metazoans), numerous species reproduce without males or sexual pairing:
   * **Bdelloid Rotifers (*Philodina roseola*, Class Bdelloidea):** Over 450 distinct species of bdelloid rotifers have persisted for more than 40 million years without a single male individual. They reproduce exclusively through obligate ameiotic parthenogenesis, maintaining genetic diversification and evolutionary adaptation without sexual pairs.
   * **New Mexico Whiptail Lizard (*Aspidoscelis neomexicanus*):** An established reptile species native to the southwestern United States that consists of 100% triploid females. Females reproduce entirely through obligate parthenogenesis, laying unfertilized eggs that develop into viable female clones without any male participation or fertilization.
   * **Brahminy Blind Snake (*Indotyphlops braminus*):** A globally distributed fossorial snake species comprising entirely female triploid individuals that reproduce exclusively through parthenogenesis. Males are absent from the species.
   * **Invertebrate Parthenogens:** Numerous species of stick insects (e.g., *Carausius morosus*), aphids, and brine shrimp (*Artemia*) reproduce without males through obligate or cyclical parthenogenesis.
5. **Fungi with Thousands of Mating Types (Multiallelic Sexes):** In the fungal kingdom, sexual reproduction frequently does not adhere to a two-sex system (*zawjayn*). The basidiomycete fungus ***Schizophyllum commune*** (the split-gill mushroom) features a tetrapolar mating system controlled by two unlinked genetic loci (*A* and *B*), each with hundreds of diverse alleles. This genetic architecture produces **over 23,000 distinct biological mating types (sexes)**. Any individual can mate with individuals of thousands of other mating types, demonstrating that reproduction in nature is not confined to a binary dual pairing.

#### Detailed Particle Physics Breakdown

1. **Self-Conjugate Fundamental Particles (No Antiparticle Pair):** Modern concordists claim that [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) anticipated Paul Dirac's AD 1928 prediction of antimatter. Dirac discovered that the relativistic wave equation for spin-1/2 fermions yields negative energy solutions corresponding to antiparticles (such as the positron for the electron). However, in quantum field theory and the Standard Model of Particle Physics, particles are described by fields subject to the charge-conjugation operator (C). When all additive quantum numbers—including electric charge (Q), baryon number (B), lepton number (L), and hypercharge (Y)—are zero, a particle can be described by a real or Hermitian field that is **strictly self-conjugate**. These particles are identical to their own antiparticles:
   * **The Photon (γ):** The fundamental gauge boson mediating the electromagnetic interaction is strictly self-conjugate. The antiparticle of a photon is the photon itself; there is no separate "anti-photon."
   * **The Neutral Z Boson (Z⁰):** The massive neutral vector boson mediating the weak neutral current is strictly self-conjugate.
   * **The Higgs Boson (H⁰):** The fundamental scalar boson responsible for electroweak symmetry breaking and the generation of particle mass is its own antiparticle.
   * **The Graviton:** In quantum gravity, the hypothetical spin-2 tensor gauge boson mediating gravitation is self-conjugate.
   * **Neutral Pions (π⁰) and η Mesons:** In hadronic physics, composite neutral mesons are their own antiparticles.
   Because these fundamental particles do not exist as pairs, but as solitary, self-identical physical states, the proposition that particle physics confirms that "all things were created in two pairs" is inconsistent with the Standard Model.
2. **Cosmological Baryon Asymmetry:** Modern cosmology demonstrates that the observable universe is not balanced into equal portions of matter and antimatter. During early cosmic baryogenesis (satisfying the Sakharov conditions, AD 1967), CP-violation and thermal non-equilibrium produced an asymmetry of approximately one excess quark per billion quark-antiquark pairs. Following annihilation, this slight asymmetry left behind the entirety of the observable universe: approximately 10⁹ photons per surviving baryon, and virtually zero primordial antimatter. The universe is characterized by pronounced matter-antimatter asymmetry rather than symmetric cosmic pairing.

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr)

Authoritative classical commentators did not interpret [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) as a description of microbiology or subatomic particle physics. Instead, they preserved early transmissions explaining that the verse refers to complementary cosmic polarities and observable natural opposites, with the theological purpose of affirming the Oneness of God:

* **Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī ([Tafsir al-Tabari 51:49](tabari://51/49)):** Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (d. AD 923) parses the grammatical construction of the verse (*wa-khalaqnā min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn, wa-turika khalaqnā al-ūlā istighnāʾan bi-dalālati al-kalām ʿalayhā*) and presents the two divergent interpretations transmitted from the earliest authorities:
  1. **Opinion 1: Polar Categories and Cosmic Opposites (*nawʿayni mukhtalifayn*):**
     * Al-Ṭabarī records from Yaʿqūb bin Ibrāhīm -> Ibn ʿUlayyah -> Ibn Jurayj -> **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** (d. AD 722, student of Ibn ʿAbbās) regarding His saying {And of all things We created pairs}:
       > *"Disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, and mankind and jinn"* (*al-kufru wa-l-īmānu, wa-l-shaqāwatu wa-l-saʿādatu, wa-l-hudā wa-l-ḍalālatu, wa-l-laylu wa-l-nahāru, wa-l-samāʾu wa-l-arḍu, wa-l-insu wa-l-jinn*).
     * Al-Ṭabarī records from Ibn Bashshār -> Ibrāhīm bin Abī al-Wazīr -> Marwān bin Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī -> ʿAwf -> **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** (d. AD 728):
       > *"The sun and the moon"* (*al-shamsu wa-l-qamar*).
  2. **Opinion 2: Male and Female in Living Creatures:**
     * Al-Ṭabarī records from Yūnus -> Ibn Wahb -> **Ibn Zayd** (d. AD 798):
       > *"A male and a female, those are the pairs. And he recited {and We made his wife fit for him} ([Quran 21:90](quran://21/90)), he said: His woman."*
  * **Al-Ṭabarī's Adjudication and Preference:** Significantly, al-Ṭabarī weighs the two views and explicitly rules that Mujāhid's interpretation of polar opposites is superior and more comprehensive than Ibn Zayd's biological reading:
    > *"And the most appropriate of the two views in this is the view of Mujāhid, which is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created for everything He created among His creation a second to it that differs from it in its meaning, so each one of them is a pair to the other, and for that reason it is said: We created pairs (`wa-awlā al-qawlayni fī dhālika qawlu Mujāhid, wa-huwa anna Allāha tabāraka wa-taʿālā khalaqa li-kulli mā khalaqa min khalqihi thāniyan lahu mukhālifan fī maʿnāhu, fa-kullu wāḥidin minhumā zawjun li-l-ākhar`)."*
  * **Al-Ṭabarī's Theological Rationale:** Al-Ṭabarī explains why God created polar opposites: inanimate elements have a single fixed nature (fire only heats and cannot cool; snow only cools and cannot heat), whereas the omnipotent Creator brings forth both a phenomenon and its opposite, demonstrating His total sovereignty:
    > *"And indeed, He, whose praise is glorious, by this saying of His merely drew attention to His capability to create whatever He wills to create of a thing, and that He is not like the things whose nature is to perform one kind of action and not its opposite, since whatever has the attribute of performing one kind of action to the exclusion of what is beside it, such as fire whose nature is heating and is not suitable for cooling, and like snow whose nature is cooling and is not suitable for heating, then it cannot permissibly be described with perfection, rather perfect praise belongs to the One capable of performing everything He wills to perform of things both different and alike. And His saying {so that you might take heed}, He says: So that you may remember and take a lesson from that. Therefore, know, O you polytheists who associate partners with Allah, that your Lord, Who deserves worship from you, is the One who is capable of creating a thing and its opposite, and of originating pairs from everything, not that which is incapable of doing so."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 51:49](tabari://51/49)).

* **Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 51:49](ibnkathir://51/49)):** ʿImād al-Dīn Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr (d. AD 1373) headlines his commentary *"All Created Things are in Pairs"* (*Jamīʿ al-makhlūqāt azwāj*), confirming the polar cosmic interpretation:
  > *"{And of everything We have created pairs} meaning: all created beings are pairs: heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, death and life, misery and happiness, Paradise and Hellfire, in addition to the animals [jinn and mankind, males and females] and plants. And for this reason He said: {that you may remember} meaning: to know that the Creator, Allah, is One without partners (`ay: li-taʿlamū anna al-khāliqa wāḥidun lā sharīka lah`)."*
  Ibn Kathīr clarifies that the theological point of the verse is *tawḥīd*: the created world is marked by duality and interdependence, while God alone is Unique, Singular, and without counterpart.

* **Classical Exegesis of [Quran 36:36](quran://36/36) ([Tafsir al-Tabari 36:36](tabari://36/36), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:36](ibnkathir://36/36)):** In their commentaries on the companion verse [Quran 36:36](quran://36/36) (*"Glory be to Him Who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know"*), al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr explain that *al-azwāj* denotes varieties and classes (*al-aṣnāf wa-l-anwāʿ*). The phrase *wa-mimmā lā yaʿlamūn* (*"and of that which they do not know"*) refers to unobserved species of animals, marine life, and plants in uncharted lands, not subatomic particle physics or cellular mitosis.

### 4. Verbatim Pre-Islamic Biblical, Jewish, Greek & Near Eastern Precedents

The proposition that [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) represents an unprecedented 7th-century formulation is not supported by the history of ancient philosophy and religious thought. The doctrine that all created entities exist in complementary pairs and polar opposites was a well-attested theological and philosophical concept circulating throughout the Near East and Mediterranean for over eight centuries prior to Islam:

* **Exact Verbatim Parallel in Ben Sira / Ecclesiasticus (2nd Century BC):** A direct lexical and conceptual precedent is found in the Wisdom of Ben Sira (Ecclesiasticus), composed in Hebrew in Jerusalem c. 180 BC and translated into Greek c. 132 BC. Ben Sira articulates the same universal premise using parallel phrasing and provides corresponding examples of polar opposites:
  * **[Sirach 42:24](bible://sir/42/24):**
    > Πάντα δισσά, ἓν κατέναντι τοῦ ἑνός, καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲν ἐλλεῖπον.
    > *"All things are in pairs, one opposite the other, and He has made nothing incomplete."*
  * **[Sirach 33:14](bible://sir/33/14)–[Sirach 33:15](bible://sir/33/15):**
    > *"[Sirach 33:14](bible://sir/33/14): Good is opposite evil, and life is opposite death; so the sinner is opposite the godly. [Sirach 33:15](bible://sir/33/15): Look upon all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, one opposite the other (δύο δύο, ἓν κατέναντι τοῦ ἑνός)."*
  The correspondence between Ben Sira and [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) is direct: [Sirach 42:24](bible://sir/42/24) (*Panta dissa, hen katenanti tou henos*, "All things are in pairs, one opposite the other") directly prefigures *wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn*. Notably, Ben Sira's specific examples of existential pairs in [Sirach 33:14](bible://sir/33/14)—good vs. evil (*agathon enanti kakou*), life vs. death (*zoe enanti thanatou*), godly vs. sinner (*eusebes enanti hamartolou*)—correspond closely to the catalog of moral and existential dualities provided by Mujāhid, al-Ṭabarī, and Ibn Kathīr (*al-kufru wa-l-īmānu, al-mawtu wa-l-ḥayātu, al-shaqāwatu wa-l-saʿādatu*).

* **Biblical and Jewish Wisdom Literature:**
  * **[Ecclesiastes 7:14](bible://ec/7/14):** *"In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after Him."* Jewish wisdom understood that God balanced human existence and the natural world with complementary counterweights.
  * **Near Eastern Cosmology:** Ancient Near Eastern cosmologies viewed the cosmos through binary frameworks: heaven and earth, upper waters and lower waters, day and night, light and darkness ([Genesis 1:3](bible://gn/1/3)).

* **Pre-Islamic Greek Polarity Philosophies:**
  * **The Pythagorean Table of Ten Opposites (*Systoichia*, 6th–5th Century BC):** As recorded by Aristotle in *Metaphysics* I.5 (986a22–26), the early Pythagoreans taught that the cosmos is constituted of ten fundamental pairs of opposites:
    1. Limit and Unlimited (*peras* / *apeiron*)
    2. Odd and Even (*peritton* / *artion*)
    3. One and Plurality (*hen* / *plethos*)
    4. Right and Left (*dexion* / *aristeron*)
    5. Male and Female (*arren* / *thelu*)
    6. Rest and Motion (*eremoun* / *kinoumenon*)
    7. Straight and Curved (*euthu* / *kampulon*)
    8. Light and Darkness (*phos* / *skotos*)
    9. Good and Evil (*agathon* / *kakon*)
    10. Square and Oblong (*tetragonon* / *heteromekes*)
  * **Heraclitus of Ephesus (c. 500 BC):** Heraclitus argued that all things exist through the dynamic tension and interchange of polar opposites (*enantiodromia*): day and night, winter and summer, war and peace, satiety and hunger (Fragments B67, B88).
  * **Empedocles (c. 490–430 BC):** Formulated a cosmology governed by two opposing cosmic principles: Love (*Philotes*), which unites disparate elements, and Strife (*Neikos*), which divides them.

* **Philo of Alexandria (*Quis Rerum Divinarum Heres*, §§ 207–214, c. 20 BC – AD 50):**
  In his philosophical treatise *Who is the Heir of Divine Things?*, the Hellenistic Jewish philosopher Philo of Alexandria analyzes the division of sacrificial offerings in [Genesis 15:10](bible://gn/15/10) and formulates an exhaustive cosmology of opposing pairs (*ta antikeimena* or *isa*). Philo demonstrates that God divided the entire cosmos into complementary pairs: heaven and earth, day and night, light and darkness, soul and body, virtue and vice. Crucially, Philo draws the identical theological conclusion found in [Tafsir al-Tabari 51:49](tabari://51/49) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 51:49](ibnkathir://51/49): God created all worldly things in pairs so that creation would acknowledge that God alone is Unpaired, Simple, and Absolute Unity (*to Hen*).

* **Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Creation, c. 3rd–6th Century AD):** In Chapter 6:3–4, this foundational Hebrew cosmological text cites [Ecclesiastes 7:14](bible://ec/7/14) and comments: *"Also God made every object, one opposite the other: good opposite evil, evil opposite good; good from good, and evil from evil; good distinguishes evil, and evil distinguishes good."*

### 5. Scholarly Evaluation of Modern Harmonizations

Modern concordist commentators propose several secondary harmonizations to align [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) with contemporary science. Each of these readings encounters significant empirical and philological difficulties when evaluated against primary sources and scientific data:

1. **The Subatomic Antimatter Harmonization ([Quran 36:36](quran://36/36) & [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49)):**
   * *The Concordist Argument:* Commentators argue that the clause *wa-mimmā lā yaʿlamūn* (*"and of that which they do not know"*) in [Quran 36:36](quran://36/36) combined with [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) anticipated Paul Dirac's AD 1928 prediction that matter is paired with antimatter.
   * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* This reading is not supported on either physical or textual grounds. In particle physics, fundamental gauge bosons mediating forces—the photon (γ), the neutral Z boson (Z⁰), the Higgs boson (H⁰), and the graviton—are strictly self-conjugate fields that act as their own antiparticles. They do not form paired physical entities. Furthermore, cosmological baryogenesis resulted in an overwhelmingly matter-dominated universe, not a dual cosmos of equal matter and antimatter pairs. Textually, early exegetes ([Tafsir al-Tabari 36:36](tabari://36/36), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 36:36](ibnkathir://36/36)) understood *wa-mimmā lā yaʿlamūn* within its natural context: uncataloged species of flora and fauna in distant, unexplored terrestrial and marine environments.
2. **Alternation Between Biological and Physical Readings:**
   * *The Concordist Argument:* Proponents alternate between biological sexual dimorphism and quantum physics depending on which empirical counterexample is under consideration.
   * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* Neither interpretive branch aligns with universal empirical findings:
     * *If interpreted biologically:* The universal premise is not sustained by taxonomic evidence. The vast majority of living organisms across evolutionary history (prokaryotic bacteria and archaea) reproduce purely through asexual binary fission without sexes. Obligate parthenogenetic animals (bdelloid rotifers for 40 million years, New Mexico whiptail lizards, Brahminy blind snakes) reproduce as 100% all-female populations without males. Fungi such as *Schizophyllum commune* possess over 23,000 distinct biological sexes rather than two pairs.
     * *If interpreted physically:* The universal premise is not sustained by quantum field theory. The gauge bosons of the Standard Model are self-conjugate and possess no distinct antiparticle mate.
3. **Dehistoricization of Ancient Near Eastern Polarity Cosmology:**
   * *The Concordist Argument:* Concordists treat the statement "We created pairs of everything" as a 20th-century scientific formulation unprecedented in ancient literature.
   * *Primary-Source & Empirical Assessment:* As demonstrated by [Sirach 42:24](bible://sir/42/24) (*"All things are in pairs, one opposite the other"*) and [Sirach 33:14](bible://sir/33/14)–[Sirach 33:15](bible://sir/33/15) written in the 2nd century BC, universal cosmic pairing was a widely circulating, standard philosophical doctrine across the Hellenistic and Semitic Near East for over eight centuries before the Quran. Early Muslim commentators (Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr) understood [Quran 51:49](quran://51/49) within this traditional framework: contrasting the observable dualities and polarities of the created universe (heaven/earth, day/night, faith/disbelief) with the solitary Oneness of God. Projecting 20th-century quantum field theory and modern biological taxonomy onto this classical theological motif diverges from both contemporary empirical science and the historical semantics of the Arabic text.

24:43.refutation:
Claims that [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) miraculously anticipated modern atmospheric physics, aircraft-altitude cumulonimbus cloud morphology, and convective charge separation rely on anachronistic reinterpretation, selective grammatical isolation, and omission of both classical exegesis and ancient literature. The passage presents an evocative, naked-eye description of a desert thunderstorm, describing God driving scattered clouds (*yuzjī saḥāban*), joining them together (*yuʾallifu baynahu*), piling them into a dense heap (*yajʿaluhu rukāman*), and bringing forth rain from their crevices (*fa-tarā al-wadqa yakhruju min khilālihi*). It then depicts hail falling from 'mountains in the sky' (*wa-yunazzilu mina al-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin*) and lightning flashing intensely (*yakādu sanā barqihi yadhhabu bi-l-abṣār*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43), [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:43](ibnkathir://24/43)) recorded two primary interpretations: (1) the literal cosmological reading, endorsed by early scholars of tafsīr (*al-mufassirūn*), that God created actual mountains of solid hail in the upper heaven from which He casts down frozen stones—a motif directly continuous with ancient Near Eastern and Biblical storehouse traditions ([Job 38:22](bible://jb/38/22), [Job 38:23](bible://jb/38/23), *1 Enoch* 41:4, *1 Enoch* 60:17–21); and (2) the metaphorical reading, in which 'mountains' refers to towering storm clouds. However, comparing towering cumulonimbus storm banks to mountain ranges is a universal naked-eye visual simile documented in Greco-Roman literature (Lucretius, *De Rerum Natura* VI.189–193, 1st century BC; Virgil, *Georgics* I.322–324, 1st century BC) and pre-Islamic Arabian poetry centuries before Islam. Furthermore, empirical cloud physics diverges from the concordist proposal that hail is required to generate lightning: the vast majority of lightning-producing storms worldwide produce zero surface hail, and non-inductive electrification occurs via microscopic ice-graupel collisions, volcanic ash plumes, and dust squalls without hail.

---

### 1. Context of Claim & Classical Arabic Philology

Following the late 20th century, concordist publications—most notably through Abdul Majeed al-Zindani's Commission on Scientific Signs in the Quran and Sunnah, Zaghloul El-Naggar, and televised lectures by Zakir Naik—claimed that [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) encapsulates modern meteorological discoveries. Proponents advance three central arguments:
1. That the Quran describes the formation of cumulonimbus storm clouds in precise developmental stages (driving, joining, piling into a heap, and raining) that are proposed to require modern radar and satellite technology to identify.
2. That the phrase *wa-yunazzilu mina al-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin* refers to towering cumulonimbus clouds whose peaks resemble mountain ranges when observed from airplanes at high altitudes.
3. That the sequence of hail followed by lightning (*yakādu sanā barqihi yadhhabu bi-l-abṣār*) presciently reveals that hail is the physical trigger and generator of lightning in the upper atmosphere.

A philological and grammatical analysis of the Quranic text demonstrates that these concordist readings are not supported by the primary text:

* **Explicit Ground-Level Naked-Eye Perspective (`A-lam tara` and `fa-tarā`):**
  The passage opens with a standard rhetorical appeal to visual observation: *a-lam tara anna Allāha yuzjī saḥāban* ("Have you not seen that Allah drives clouds..."). It continues by stating: *fa-tarā al-wadqa yakhruju min khilālihi* ("and you see the rain emerging from within it"). The verbs *tara* and *tarā* are second-person singular imperfect forms of *raʾā* (to see visually with physical sight). The text explicitly appeals to the direct, naked-eye sensory experience of a 7th-century Arabian observer standing on the ground during a desert storm.
  Across flat Arabian desert plains, a towering convective storm cloud (cumulonimbus) rising 10 to 18 kilometers into the troposphere is visible against the clear horizon from distances exceeding 150 to 200 kilometers. The observer directly witnesses the wind propelling scattered, low-level cumulus clouds (*yuzjī saḥāban*), merging them into a unified storm bank (*yuʾallifu baynahu*), piling them vertically into a dense mass (*yajʿaluhu rukāman*), and releasing visible rain shafts and virga curtains beneath the base (*fa-tarā al-wadqa yakhruju min khilālihi*). This visual progression was universally observed by ancient pastoralists worldwide.

* **Classical Philology of the Three Prepositions (`Min`) and Syntactic Gender Agreement:**
  The pivotal clause reads: *wa-yunazzilu mina al-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin* (وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِنْ بَرَدٍ). Classical Arabic grammarians (including al-Farrāʾ, d. AD 822; al-Zajjāj, d. AD 923; al-Zamakhsharī, d. AD 1144; and Ibn Kathīr, d. AD 1373) analyzed the syntactical role of the three successive occurrences of the preposition *min*:
  1. *Mina al-samāʾ* (مِنَ السَّمَاءِ): The initial *min* signifies spatial origin or the commencement of distance (*li-ibtidāʾ al-ghāyah*), indicating that precipitation descends from the upper celestial vault.
  2. *Min jibālin* (مِنْ جِبَالٍ): In the primary classical exegetical reading, this second *min* is partitive (*li-l-tabʿīḍ*) or denotes a secondary spatial origin, signifying that within heaven there exist solid mountains from which portions of hail are detached and cast down. Under the metaphorical reading, this second *min* is an appositive substitute (*badal*) for the first, treating the clouds themselves as mountains.
  3. *Min barad* (مِنْ بَرَدٍ): The third *min* functions as an explanation of genus or composition (*li-bayān al-jins*), defining what the celestial mountains consist of—specifically, hail. Hence the literal translation: *"And He sends down from the sky, from mountains within it consisting of hail."*

* **The Syntactic Significance of the Feminine Pronoun `fīhā` (فِيهَا):**
  Crucially, the prepositional phrase *fīhā* ("in it" / "within it") contains a feminine singular pronominal suffix (*-hā*). In Arabic grammar, *al-samāʾ* (the sky/heaven) is grammatically feminine (*muʾannath samāʿī*). By contrast, *al-saḥāb* (clouds) in this verse is grammatically treated as masculine singular (*mudhakkar*), as shown by the surrounding masculine pronouns: *baynahu* (بَيْنَهُ, masculine singular), *yajʿaluhu* (يَجْعَلُهُ, masculine singular), and *khilālihi* (خِلَالِهِ, masculine singular).
  If the Quranic author had intended to state that mountains of hail exist *inside the clouds*, classical Arabic syntax would have strictly required the masculine suffix *fīhi* (فِيهِ). The employment of the feminine *fīhā* grammatically binds the mountains to *al-samāʾ* (the celestial heaven). Syntactically, the clause states that within the celestial sky (*fī al-samāʾ*), there are mountains composed of hail.

* **Grammatical Referent of `Sanā Barqihi` (سَنَا بَرْقِهِ):**
  The verse concludes: *yakādu sanā barqihi yadhhabu bi-l-abṣār* ("The flash of its/His lightning almost takes away the sight"). The pronominal suffix *-hi* is masculine singular. Classical commentators identified two primary grammatical referents: (a) *al-saḥāb* (the cloud mass), designating the intense lightning generated within the cloud, or (b) *Allāh*, designating the lightning belonging to God, or (c) *al-barad* (the hail), indicating the dazzling reflection of light from falling ice. In classical grammar, the phrase describes the simultaneous visual hazards of the tempest, rather than positing an atmospheric electrochemical theory that hail causes lightning.

### 2. Meteorological & Empirical Analysis (With Markdown Comparison Table)

Modern atmospheric physics and observational meteorology present an empirical framework that diverges from both the literal cosmological reading of [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) and modern concordist reinterpretations:

| Meteorological Phenomenon | Modern Empirical Atmospheric Science | Quranic Account & Concordist Claims ([Quran 24:43](quran://24/43)) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Origin & Structure of Hail (Barad)** | Hail forms dynamically inside convective storm updrafts when supercooled liquid water droplets (-10°C to -30°C) rime onto frozen ice embryos, falling when updrafts cannot suspend their mass. No static masses of ice exist in the sky. | [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) depicts hail descending from "mountains in the sky" (*min jibālin fīhā min baradin*), which early scholars of tafsīr ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43)) understood as literal celestial mountains of hail created in the firmament. |
| **Visual Perspective on Cloud Mountains** | Cumulonimbus calvus and incus clouds tower 12 to 18 km vertically. Their mountain-like turrets, sheer vertical walls, and anvil crests are readily visible to naked-eye ground observers over 150 km away across flat terrain. | Concordists claim the mountain simile requires modern aviation viewpoints. Historically, Lucretius (1st century BC) and pre-Islamic poets described towering clouds as resembling mountain crags from ground level. |
| **Precipitation Dynamics (Al-Wadq & Rukām)** | Cloud droplets condense around microscopic aerosol cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) via adiabatic cooling during convective ascent. Collision-coalescence produces raindrops without requiring pre-existing static heaps. | Concordists assert the sequence of driving, joining, and piling anticipates modern cloud physics; however, wind assembling scattered scud clouds into a storm bank is a directly observable naked-eye meteorological phenomenon. |
| **Lightning Electrification vs. Hail** | Lightning occurs in millions of thunderstorms, volcanic plumes, and sandstorms that produce zero hail. Triboelectric charging operates between small ice crystals and light graupel pellets, not large hailstones. | Concordists argue the sequence "hail... lightning" reveals hail causes lightning. Meteorologically, hail is neither necessary nor sufficient for lightning, and most lightning storms worldwide produce no hail. |
| **Distribution of Hail Precipitation** | Hail falls along narrow convective corridors ("hailswaths") determined entirely by mesoscale updraft strength, mid-level freezing altitude, and storm propagation vector. | The verse attributes hail distribution to localized divine targeting (*fa-yuṣību bihi man yashāʾ wa-yaṣrifuhu ʿan man yashāʾ*), reflecting ancient theological concepts of punitive weather. |

#### Detailed Physical Analysis of Atmospheric Mechanics

1. **Dynamic Hail Formation vs. Static Celestial Mountains:**
   In cloud physics, hail is an ephemeral kinetic product of severe convective storm cells (cumulonimbus). Hailstones originate from frozen raindrops or graupel particles (embryos) suspended inside strong updrafts where vertical air velocities range from 15 to over 45 meters per second. In the mixed-phase zone of the cloud, where temperatures range between -10°C and -30°C, supercooled liquid water droplets collide with and freeze onto the embryos through accretional riming. The growing hailstones cycle through regions of varying liquid water content, developing alternating layers of opaque rime ice and transparent clear ice. Once the hailstone's gravitational weight exceeds the aerodynamic drag of the updraft, it falls toward the surface. At no point in atmospheric physics do stationary, solid "mountains of hail" exist in the upper atmosphere. The literal exegetical understanding recorded in classical tafsīr represents an ancient cosmological framework rather than observational atmospheric physics.

2. **Ground Visibility of Convective Cloud "Mountains":**
   Concordist writers assert that humans could only perceive cumulonimbus clouds as resembling mountains from high-altitude aircraft. This argument does not account for standard atmospheric optics and horizon geometry. A mature cumulonimbus incus cloud regularly extends from a base of 1,000 meters to an anvil top between 12,000 and 18,000 meters (40,000 to 60,000 feet), extending to the tropopause. Because the Earth is a sphere, the geometric distance to the horizon ($d$) for an elevated cloud summit is given by $d \approx 3.57 \times \sqrt{h}$ kilometers. For a storm cloud summit 15,000 meters high, the cloud top is theoretically visible to an observer on flat ground from over 430 kilometers away, and easily visible with clear contrast at distances of 100 to 200 kilometers.
   In arid and semi-arid landscapes such as the Arabian Peninsula, where atmospheric humidity is low and visibility is exceptionally clear, towering cumulonimbus clouds rising above the desert horizon appear visually similar to snow-capped mountain massifs. Nomadic desert dwellers observing these towering white anvils and craggy towers from the ground naturally compared them to mountain ranges.

3. **Atmospheric Electrification Mechanics vs. Macroscopic Hail:**
   Modern concordist writing frequently claims that [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) anticipated modern atmospheric electricity by mentioning hail immediately before the flash of lightning. This claim is inconsistent with empirical findings:
   * *Global Dissociation of Hail and Lightning:* The vast majority of thunderstorms on Earth that generate prolific lightning produce zero surface hail. In the tropical regions of central Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Amazon Basin—which experience the highest lightning flash densities on the planet (e.g., Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela, with over 200 thunderstorm days per year)—surface hail is exceptionally rare. This occurs because the tropical freezing level is high (typically 4.5 to 5.0 km above sea level), ensuring that any frozen hydrometeors melt completely into rain long before reaching the ground. If hail were required for lightning, tropical thunderstorms would be incapable of generating electrical discharges.
   * *The Non-Inductive Charging Mechanism:* In modern thunderstorm electrification physics (Reynolds et al., 1957; Takahashi, 1978; Saunders, 1991), macroscopic hailstones (defined as frozen precipitation $\ge 5$ mm in diameter) play no essential role in charge generation. Instead, charge separation occurs through non-inductive triboelectric charging during collisions between microscopic ice crystals (sizes $\sim 10$ to $100$ micrometers) and soft, millimeter-sized graupel pellets (rimed snow grains) in the presence of supercooled liquid droplets at temperatures between -10°C and -25°C. The lighter ice crystals gain positive charge and are carried to the upper anvil by updrafts, while the denser graupel pellets acquire negative charge and settle in the mid-levels of the storm, establishing the dominant tripole electrical structure of the thunderstorm. Large hailstones are an incidental byproduct of strong updrafts, not the causal mechanism of electrical breakdown.
   * *Lightning Devoid of Hail and Ice:* Intense electrical discharges and lightning flashes occur routinely in environments that lack water ice and hail altogether, such as volcanic eruption plumes (volcanic lightning generated by fracto-emission and triboelectric charging of silicate ash particles) and convective dust storms (sandstorm electrification).

4. **Meteorological Hailswaths vs. Divine Targeted Smiting:**
   The verse states that God strikes with hail whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills (*fa-yuṣību bihi man yashāʾ wa-yaṣrifuhu ʿan man yashāʾ*). In physical meteorology, hail falls in narrow, localized swaths typically 2 to 10 kilometers wide and 10 to 40 kilometers long, governed strictly by the storm cell's mesocyclone tilt, updraft dissipation dynamics, and forward cell motion. Ancient populations observing hail destroy crops in one village while leaving an adjacent orchard undamaged interpreted this localized meteorological footprint as purposeful, moral punishment rather than a normal physical feature of convective downdrafts.

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr)

Early Islamic tradition and authoritative classical commentaries did not interpret [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) as a description of aircraft-altitude cloud morphology or cloud electrification. Classical exegetes documented two main positions: literal celestial mountains of hail, or a poetic metaphor for immense clouds, both viewed strictly from the ground:

* **Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43)):**
  Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (d. AD 923) provides an extensive compilation of early interpretations regarding each clause of the verse:
  * *The Driving and Piling of Clouds:* Al-Ṭabarī records the tradition of the early scholar ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī outlining the traditional Arabian conception of the four winds:
    *"The winds are four: Allah sends the first wind, and it sweeps the earth completely; then He sends the second, and it originates clouds; then He sends the third, and it gathers them and makes them into a heap (rukām); then He sends the fourth, and it makes them rain."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43)).
  * *The Rain Emerging from Gaps:* Regarding *fa-tarā al-wadqa yakhruju min khilālihi*, al-Ṭabarī cites Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who recited *min khalalihi* ("from its gaps/fissures"), explaining that *al-wadq* is rain emerging through crevices between clouds. He cites the pre-Islamic poet ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn al-Ṭāʾī: *"No cloud poured down its rain (wadqahā), and no earth sprouted its vegetation."*
  * *Literal Mountains of Hail in Heaven:* When addressing *wa-yunazzilu mina al-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin*, al-Ṭabarī explicitly documents the two competing opinions among the early generations (*Salaf*):
    *"And two opinions were said regarding that. One of them is: that its meaning is that Allah sends down from the sky, from mountains of hail in the sky created right there, which He created; as if the mountains, according to this opinion, are of hail, just as it is said: 'mountains of clay'. And the other opinion is: that Allah sends down from the sky the measure of mountains, and the likes of mountains of hail to the earth, just as it is said: 'I have two houses of straw', meaning the measure of two houses of straw, while the two houses are not made of straw."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43)).
  * *Punitive Smiting:* Explaining *fa-yuṣību bihi man yashāʾ*, al-Ṭabarī writes: *"He punishes with that which He sends down from the sky, from mountains in which there is hail, whomever He wills, thus destroying him, or destroying his crops and his wealth with it; and He turns it away from whomever He pleases from His creation, meaning from their crops and their wealth."* ([Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43)).
  * *The Lightning Flash:* Citing Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd, al-Ṭabarī confirms that *sanā barqihi* means the radiant brilliance of the cloud's lightning flash (*ḍawʾu barqihi*).

* **Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:43](ibnkathir://24/43)):**
  Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr (d. AD 1373) details the grammatical analysis of the three *min* prepositions and evaluates early scholarly views:
  * *Grammatical Analysis of the Prepositions:*
    *"Some of the grammarians said: The first 'min' is to initiate the limit [origin], the second is for the partitive, and the third is to explain the kind [genus]. This applies according to the view of those scholars of Tafsir who say that His saying: {from mountains in it of hail} means: that in the sky there are mountains of hail from which Allah sends down hail. As for those who make 'mountains' here a metaphor for clouds, the second 'min' in their view is also to initiate the limit, but it is a substitute for the first. And Allah knows best."* ([Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:43](ibnkathir://24/43)).
  * Ibn Kathīr acknowledges that the primary literal reading among early mufassirūn was that physical mountains of hail exist in the celestial vault. The alternative metaphorical reading was understood not as an anticipation of modern atmospheric science, but as a standard visual simile comparing huge storm clouds to mountains.

### 4. Verbatim Pre-Islamic Classical, Biblical & Apocalyptic Precedents

Both elements of [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43)—the cosmological belief in heavenly storehouses or mountains of hail, and the poetic comparison of towering clouds to mountain ranges—were widespread throughout the ancient Near East and Mediterranean world centuries before Islam:

* **Cosmological Storehouses of Hail in Biblical and Apocalyptic Literature:**
  In ancient Hebrew and Second Temple Jewish literature, precipitation elements such as hail, snow, and wind were conceived as stored within physical chambers, treasuries, or mountains located inside the celestial firmament:
  * **[Job 38:22](bible://jb/38/22)–[Job 38:23](bible://jb/38/23)** (composed c. 6th–5th century BC): God challenges Job regarding the physical construction of heaven:
    *"Have you entered into the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail (*otzrot barad*), which I have reserved for the time of distress, for the day of war and battle?"*
  * **[Joshua 10:11](bible://jo/10/11)**: God rains down massive stones of hail from heaven to destroy the enemies of Israel:
    *"The Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them to Azekah, and they died; there were more who died with the hailstones than whom the children of Israel slew with the sword."*
  * **[Psalm 135:7](bible://ps/135/7)** and **[Jeremiah 10:13](bible://jer/10/13)**:
    *"He causes the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain; He brings forth the wind out of His treasuries."*
  * **[Revelation 16:21](bible://rv/16/21)**: Celestial judgment in the form of massive hailstones falling from the sky:
    *"And great hail out of heaven, every stone about the weight of a talent, fell upon men..."*
  * **Second Temple Jewish Apocalyptic Literature (*1 Enoch*, c. 3rd–1st century BC):**
    In *1 Enoch* 41:4 and *1 Enoch* 60:17–21, the firmament contains literal storehouses and chambers for hail, snow, and frost:
    *"And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds..."* (*1 Enoch* 41:4) and *"And the spirit of the hoar-frost is his own angel, and the spirit of the hail is a good angel. And the spirit of the snow has forsaken his chambers on account of his strength... And the spirit of the mist is not united with them in their chambers, but it has a special chamber..."* (*1 Enoch* 60:17–19).
    The literal exegetical view documented by al-Ṭabarī—that God created actual mountains of hail in the celestial sky—is an inheritance of this ancient Near Eastern storehouse cosmology.

* **Greco-Roman Literature: Towering Clouds Compared to Mountains:**
  Classical authors writing centuries before Islam frequently described storm clouds as towering mountain ranges from their ground observations:
  * **Lucretius (*De Rerum Natura* VI.189–193, c. 55 BC):**
    The Roman poet-philosopher Lucretius explicitly noted that winds pile up clouds that resemble mountains:
    *"Contemplator enim, cum montibus adsimulata / nubila portabunt venti transversa per auras, / aut ubi per magnos montis cumulata videbis / insuper esse aliis alia atque urguere superne / in statione locata sepultis undique ventis."*
    (*"For behold, when the winds carry clouds resembling mountains across through the air, or when you see them piled upon great mountains, one above another, and pressing down from on high, stationed there while the winds are buried all around."*).
    Lucretius's phrase *montibus adsimulata nubila* ("clouds resembling mountains") demonstrates that comparing clouds to mountains did not require modern aerial observation.
  * **Aristophanes (*Clouds* 323–326, 423 BC):**
    Socrates directs Strepsiades to look toward Mount Parnes to observe the clouds gathering and descending slowly in dense masses across the mountain hollows and thickets (*dia tōn koilōn kai tōn daseōn*).
  * **Virgil (*Georgics* I.322–324, 1st century BC):**
    Virgil depicts dark storm clouds gathering on high and massing into a tempest as the lofty sky rushes down in torrents (*et foedam glomerant tempestatem imbribus atris / collectae ex alto nubes; ruit arduus aether*).
  * **Aristotle (*Meteorologica* I.12, 347b–348b, c. 340 BC) and Seneca (*Naturales Quaestiones* IVb.3, c. AD 65):**
    Aristotle analyzed hail formation inside dense clouds, explaining that moisture is condensed and rapidly frozen when driven into intensely cold upper regions. Seneca similarly described hail as frozen moisture formed within dense cloud masses.

* **Pre-Islamic Arabian Poetry (*Jāhiliyyah*, 6th Century AD):**
  In pre-Islamic Arabia, nomadic poets constantly observed convective thunderstorms on the desert horizon. Towering storm clouds (*saḥāb rukām*) were standard literary motifs:
  * **Imruʾ al-Qays (Muʿallaqah, lines 71–76, 6th century AD):**
    In the celebrated pre-Islamic ode, Imruʾ al-Qays depicts how the desert storm cloud's torrential downpour envelops the peak of Mount Thabīr on the horizon like an elder wrapped in a striped cloak: *ka-anna Thabīran fī ʿarānīni wablihi / kabīru unāsin fī bijādin muzammalī* ("As though the peak of Mount Thabīr, amidst the foremost downpour of its rain, were an elder of the people wrapped in a striped cloak").
  * **ʿAbīd ibn al-Abraṣ (Diwan, 6th century AD):**
    The poet describes convective storm clouds (*al-saḥāb al-murtakim*) rising like towering mountain peaks (*aʿlām* or *jibāl*), driven by winds across the desert before discharging heavy rain and hail.
  * **Aws ibn Ḥajar (Diwan, 6th century AD):**
    Aws depicts thunderclouds heaped like dark mountain peaks (*ka-l-jibāl*), flashing with continuous lightning and pelting the stony desert with hail.

### 5. Scholarly Evaluation of Modern Harmonizations

Modern concordist writers advance three primary arguments to align [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) with contemporary atmospheric science. Each argument encounters substantial philological, physical, and historical difficulties:

* **1. Evaluation of the Aerial Perspective Hypothesis:**
  Concordist commentators assert that cumulonimbus clouds appear like mountain ranges only when viewed from an aircraft at cruising altitudes, concluding that a 7th-century author could not have produced this comparison without divine inspiration. This proposal is inconsistent with optical geometry and historical attestations:
  * As demonstrated by Lucretius in 55 BC (*"clouds resembling mountains"*), Aristophanes in 423 BC, Virgil (*Georgics* I.322–324) in the 1st century BC, and pre-Islamic poets like Imruʾ al-Qays, ʿAbīd ibn al-Abraṣ, and Aws ibn Ḥajar, observing towering storm clouds and their interaction with mountain peaks from the ground was an established literary and descriptive trope across antiquity.
  * Due to the curvature of the Earth and the vast vertical extent of cumulonimbus clouds (rising 12 to 18 km), these cloud formations present vertical relief and craggy silhouettes that are visible to ground observers over 150 km away across open desert terrain. Ground observers had no need for aircraft to perceive towering storm clouds as mountains.

* **2. Evaluation of the Grammatical Harmonization (Syntactic Gender Agreement):**
  To avoid the scientific difficulty of literal mountains of ice stationed in the sky, concordist writers reinterpret *min jibālin fīhā min baradin* to mean "from clouds that are like mountains containing hail". This reading diverges from classical Arabic grammar:
  * Throughout the first half of [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43), *al-saḥāb* (clouds) is treated as grammatically masculine: *baynahu* (بَيْنَهُ, masculine singular), *yajʿaluhu* (يَجْعَلُهُ, masculine singular), and *khilālihi* (خِلَالِهِ, masculine singular).
  * In the clause *wa-yunazzilu mina al-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin*, the prepositional phrase *fīhā* (فِيهَا) contains the feminine singular suffix *-hā*.
  * In Arabic syntax, *al-samāʾ* (sky/heaven) is grammatically feminine, whereas *al-saḥāb* is here treated as masculine.
  * Therefore, the pronoun *-hā* in *fīhā* grammatically refers back to *al-samāʾ*, not *al-saḥāb*. The sentence states: *"He sends down from the sky, from mountains within it [the sky] consisting of hail."* This syntactic structure led early scholars of tafsīr (*al-mufassirūn*) cited in [Tafsir al-Tabari 24:43](tabari://24/43) and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:43](ibnkathir://24/43) to conclude that the text speaks of literal mountains of hail stationed in the celestial heavens, corresponding to the storehouses of ancient Near Eastern cosmology.

* **3. Evaluation of the Hail-Induced Lightning Hypothesis (`Sanā Barqihi`):**
  Concordists argue that the proximity of hail and lightning in [Quran 24:43](quran://24/43) anticipates the discovery that hail induces lightning electrification. This hypothesis is not supported on either empirical or textual grounds:
  * In atmospheric physics, hail is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition for lightning. The vast majority of lightning-producing storms globally—including nearly all tropical convective squalls—produce zero hail at ground level. Lightning charge generation operates via non-inductive collisions between microscopic ice crystals and soft graupel pellets, not large hailstones. Furthermore, lightning occurs in completely dry volcanic ash clouds and sandstorms.
  * Textually, hail and lightning are paired because they represent the most conspicuous and destructive sensory elements of severe thunderstorms observed by human populations. Ancient observers did not require a modern theory of microphysical triboelectric charge transfer to observe that severe hailstorms are accompanied by bright lightning flashes.

24:40.refutation:
Claims that [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40) miraculously anticipated 20th-century oceanography by describing internal oceanic waves (*mawj min fawqihi mawj*) and the layered optical attenuation of deep seawater rely on semantic reinterpretation, selective literalism, and assumptions inconsistent with empirical marine physics. In modern physical oceanography, internal gravity waves oscillate along subsurface density interfaces (the pycnocline or thermocline, typically 50 to 200 meters below the surface); they are optically transparent fluids undulating beneath fluids of differing density that do not block downwelling sunlight, cast shadows, or produce layers of darkness. Furthermore, the oceanic aphotic zone—the realm of permanent, total pitch-blackness below 1,000 meters—exists 24 hours a day under cloudless, sunny midday skies due to the continuous exponential attenuation of solar photons ($I(z) = I_0 e^{-K_d z}$), and is completely unaffected by whether storm clouds exist in the atmosphere above.

By contrast, [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40) does not describe a deep-sea submersible or bathypelagic abyss. It presents an evocative moral parable comparing the compounded spiritual ignorance of the unrepentant disbeliever to an endangered mariner engulfed in a violent, overcast nighttime tempest at sea: `أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا` (*"Or like darknesses in a deep sea: a wave covers it, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud—darknesses, some of them above others; when he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it"*). In this dramatic scene, the three compounding macroscopic barriers to light are explicitly identified: (1) the dark, churning surface water, (2) the towering, cresting storm waves, and (3) the thick, sun-blocking storm clouds overhead. This storm-at-sea topos was a standard literary convention across pre-Islamic Arabian poetry, the Hebrew Bible ([Jonah 2:3](bible://jon/2/3), [Psalm 107:25](bible://ps/107/25)), and classical Greco-Roman maritime epics (Homer, Virgil), where billows crash upon billows beneath black storm clouds.

### 1. Context of Claim & Classical Arabic Philology

Following the establishment of the Commission on Scientific Signs in the Quran and Sunnah in Saudi Arabia during the AD 1980s by Abdul Majeed al-Zindani, concordist authors (including oceanographer Dr. M. Rao, Zakir Naik, and Harun Yahya) began claiming that the verse `كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ` in [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40) contains dual oceanographic miracles:
1. *Internal Waves:* Proponents assert that the phrase `مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ` (*mawjun min fawqihi mawj*, "a wave, above which is a wave") presciently refers to internal waves discovered along oceanic pycnoclines and thermoclines in the 20th century, which move along the subsurface boundary between water layers of different densities, overlaid by surface waves.
2. *Deep-Sea Layered Darkness:* Proponents argue that `بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ` (*baḥrin lujjiyyin*, "a deep sea") and `ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ` (*ẓulumātun baʿḍuhā fawqa baʿḍ*, "darknesses, some of them above others") describe the photic, dysphotic (twilight), and aphotic zones below 200–1,000 meters, where different wavelengths of solar light are sequentially absorbed until total darkness reigns, preventing a deep-sea diver from seeing his outstretched hand (`إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا`).

A rigorous philological and syntactical analysis of [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40) in classical Arabic lexicography demonstrates that this concordist reading diverges from the grammatical structure of the text:

* **Classical Arabic Lexicography of *Baḥr Lujjiyy* (`بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ`):** In foundational classical dictionaries (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn* by al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, d. AD 786; *al-Ṣiḥāḥ* by al-Jawharī, d. AD 1003; *Lisān al-ʿArab* by Ibn Manẓūr, d. AD 1312; *Lane's Lexicon*, Book I, p. 2664), *lujjah* (لُجّة) denotes the vast, surging expanse or main body of water (*muʿẓam al-māʾ*), where waters billow and roll together. The relative adjective *lujjiyy* describes a vast, open, deep sea characterized by churning waves, as opposed to shallow shoals (*ḍaḥḍāḥ*) or coastal bays. Al-Khalīl defines *iltajja al-baḥr* as: "the sea became violent and its waves clashed together."
* **Syntax and Object of *Yaghshāhu Mawjun* (`يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ`):** In classical Arabic grammar, the transitive verb *ghashiya* / *yaghshā* signifies to cover, overspread, or envelop something from above. In the phrase *yaghshāhu mawjun*, the attached 3rd-person masculine singular objective pronoun (*damīr al-mafʿūl bihi* `-hu`) refers directly back to the preceding masculine noun: `بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ` (*baḥrin lujjiyyin*, "a deep sea"). Syntactically, this means: "a wave overspreads and covers the [surface of the] sea." The first wave is therefore located **on top of the sea's surface**, not hundreds of meters beneath it in the subsurface interior water column.
* **The Idiom *Mawjun min Fawqihi Mawjun min Fawqihi Saḥāb* (`يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ`):** In classical Arabic maritime descriptions, the prepositional construction *min fawqihi* ("above it") denotes physical stacking or rapid, surging succession. "A wave above which is another wave" is an idiomatic depiction of successive, towering surface storm waves crashing one over another during a violent tempest. Parallel Quranic passages confirm that the Quran consistently depicts heavy maritime storms as towering waves that envelop seafaring vessels:
  * **[Quran 10:22](quran://10/22):** *"...until when you are in ships, and they sail with them with a fair breeze, and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the wave comes upon them from every side (`jāʾahumu al-mawju min kulli makān`)."*
  * **[Quran 11:42](quran://11/42):** *"And it sailed with them through waves like mountains (`fī mawjin ka-l-jibāl`)."*
  * **[Quran 31:32](quran://31/32):** *"And when a wave covers them like canopies (`wa-idhā ghashiyahum mawjun ka-l-ẓulal`)."*
* **The Three Layers of Darkness (*Ẓulumātun Baʿḍuhā Fawqa Baʿḍ*, `ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ`):** The verse itself provides the explicit cause of the stacked darknesses: the sea, the wave, and the clouds (*min fawqihi saḥāb*, `سَحَابٌ`). As demonstrated unanimously in classical exegesis, these are the three macroscopic, physical layers of darkness in a nighttime squall: (1) the darkness of the deep water, (2) the darkness of the towering waves, and (3) the darkness of the thick storm clouds obscuring the sky, augmented by the darkness of the night. It is this combined atmospheric and maritime tempest that causes an endangered person on the water to be unable to discern his own outstretched hand (`إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا`, *idhā akhraja yadahu lam yakad yarāhā*).

### 2. Oceanographic & Optical Empirical Analysis (With Markdown Comparison Table)

Modern physical oceanography and empirical optics establish that the physical mechanisms governing internal waves, oceanic light attenuation, and bathyal darkness have no correlation with the atmospheric storm imagery described in [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40):

| Oceanographic Parameter | Modern Physical Oceanography & Empirical Optics | Concordist Claim | Quranic Reality ([Quran 24:40](quran://24/40)) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Location & Physical Boundary of Waves** | Internal waves occur *beneath* the surface along subsurface density discontinuities (pycnoclines or thermoclines, typically 50–200 m deep) within the stratified fluid column. | The lower wave is an internal wave at the pycnocline; the upper wave is the surface wave. | The first wave explicitly covers and overspreads the surface of the sea (*yaghshāhu mawj*), with a second storm wave crashing above it, beneath storm clouds. |
| **Optical Transparency vs. Light Blocking** | Internal gravity waves consist of transparent seawater undulating against slightly denser seawater. They do not block, scatter, or absorb sunlight, nor do they cast shadows or create darkness. | Internal waves cause the dark, layered divisions of oceanic light. | Waves and storm clouds are enumerated as the physical light-blocking barriers that create compounding darkness (*ẓulumāt*). |
| **Mechanism of Oceanic Darkness** | Seawater absorbs solar radiation continuously and exponentially via the Beer-Lambert law ($I(z) = I_0 e^{-K_d z}$). It is a continuous logarithmic decay across the spectrum, not discrete layered partitions. | "Darkness upon darkness" refers to the separate absorption layers of the color spectrum (red, orange, green, blue). | The darknesses are macroscopic environmental obstacles: the water body, the crashing waves, and the thick atmospheric clouds. |
| **Role of Atmospheric Storm Clouds (Saḥāb)** | The bathypelagic aphotic zone (below 1,000 m) is permanently 100% pitch-black at midday under cloudless sunny skies. Atmospheric storm clouds 1 km above have zero optical effect on the abyss. | Describes the permanent darkness of the deep ocean aphotic zone. | Atmospheric storm clouds (*saḥāb*) directly overhead are required to produce the darkness, confirming a surface storm context. |
| **Human Physiological Context** | Below 200–1,000 meters, hydrostatic pressure exceeds 20 to 100 atmospheres (~2,000–10,000 kPa). An unprotected human would be instantly crushed and killed without high-pressure diving submersibles. | A human swimmer or diver stretching out his hand and failing to see it at great oceanic depths. | Depicts a mariner or swimmer in a surface storm extending his hand in the pitch-black night and struggling to see it against the tempest. |

#### Detailed Breakdown of the Physical Oceanographic Evidence

1. **Physical Mechanics of Internal Gravity Waves:** In fluid dynamics and oceanography, internal waves are gravity waves that oscillate within a continuously stratified fluid medium or along a sharp pycnocline (a boundary separating water masses of differing temperature, salinity, and density). While their vertical amplitudes can reach tens of meters, they are entirely subsurface phenomena driven by the Brunt-Väisälä buoyancy frequency ($N = \sqrt{-(g/\rho)(\partial\rho/\partial z)}$). Crucially, internal waves do not cover the ocean surface; they propagate beneath the mixed layer. In [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40), the grammar states that the first wave covers the sea itself (*yaghshāhu mawj*), and above this wave is another wave, topped by atmospheric clouds (*saḥāb*). This represents surface wave superposition—breaking storm seas (*seas and swells*) crashing over each other in a gale.
2. **Optical Transparency of Internal Waves:** Concordist literature claims that internal waves create deep oceanic darkness. This claim is inconsistent with optical physics. Water across a pycnocline exhibits an index of refraction change of less than 0.001 (e.g., between fresh and saline, or warm and cold water). Internal waves are optically transparent. Downwelling solar photons pass through an internal wave with virtually identical transmittance as through unstratified water. Internal waves do not create darkness, do not form an optical boundary, and cannot cause "layers of darkness."
3. **The Beer-Lambert Law vs. Discrete Light Layers:** Sunlight penetrating the ocean attenuates according to the Beer-Lambert law:
   $$I(z) = I_0 e^{-K_d z}$$
   where $I(z)$ is the downwelling irradiance at depth $z$, $I_0$ is the surface irradiance, and $K_d$ is the diffuse vertical attenuation coefficient for downwelling irradiance (varying by wavelength $\lambda$). Long wavelengths (infrared and red light, $\lambda \approx 650\text{--}700\text{ nm}$) have large attenuation coefficients and are absorbed within the first 5 to 15 meters, converting into heat. Shorter wavelengths (blue-green light, $\lambda \approx 450\text{--}490\text{ nm}$) penetrate deepest in clear open-ocean waters (up to 200 meters in the mesopelagic twilight zone). However, this attenuation is a smooth, continuous exponential gradient across the entire water column. There are no discrete "darknesses stacked upon darknesses" separating the water into stepped shelves.
4. **The Aphotic Zone and Atmospheric Clouds:** The bathypelagic aphotic zone (depths greater than 1,000 meters) is completely devoid of sunlight under all meteorological conditions. Whether the sky above the ocean is brilliantly sunny at noon or covered by storm clouds makes no difference to a depth of 1,000 meters: zero solar photons reach that depth. In [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40), however, the presence of thick storm clouds (*min fawqihi saḥāb*) is an essential component of the darkness. If the verse were describing the deep aphotic ocean, mentioning overhead storm clouds would be scientifically irrelevant. The inclusion of clouds confirms that the text depicts a surface storm where thick overcast skies extinguish moonlight and starlight.

### 3. Classical Islamic Exegesis (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī & Ibn Kathīr)

Classical commentators and the earliest companions of Muhammad unanimously recognized that [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40) is an allegorical simile (*tamthīl*) for the compounded ignorance, blindness, and spiritual ruin of the disbeliever. It was never understood as an empirical disclosure of subsurface ocean physics:

* **The Twin Parables of Surah an-Nur ([Quran 24:39](quran://24/39) and [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40)):** As explained by both al-Ṭabarī in [Tafsir al-Tabari 24:40](tabari://24/40) and Ibn Kathīr in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:40](ibnkathir://24/40), these two contiguous verses present twin allegories for two distinct categories of disbelievers:
  * **The Active Deceivers in Compound Ignorance ([Quran 24:39](quran://24/39)):** The defiant leaders of disbelief who perform deeds falsely imagining they have value—whom Ibn Kathīr explicitly categorizes as possessing **compound ignorance** (`ذَوِي الْجَهْلِ الْمُرَكَّبِ`, *dhawī al-jahl al-murakkab*, those who are ignorant yet imagine they possess knowledge)—are compared to a desert mirage (*sarāb bi-qīʿah*). When the thirsty traveler reaches it, he finds nothing, but finds God ready to settle his account.
  * **The Blind Imitators in Simple Ignorance ([Quran 24:40](quran://24/40)):** The unthinking followers who blindly imitate the leaders of disbelief without insight—whom Ibn Kathīr explicitly categorizes in [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 24:40](ibnkathir://24/40) as the people of **simple ignorance** (`أَصْحَابُ الْجَهْلِ الْبَسِيطِ`, *aṣḥāb al-jahl al-basīṭ*, describing the heart of the blind imitator, `قَلْبِ الْكَافِرِ الْجَاهِلِ الْبَسِيطِ الْمُقَلِّدِ`)—are compared to a man engulfed in a deep, dark sea storm, completely blind to where he is being led.
* **Early Exegetical Consensus in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī:** In [Tafsir al-Tabari 24:40](tabari://24/40), Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī records the chains of transmission from the earliest authorities:
  * **Ubayy ibn Kaʿb:** Al-Ṭabarī narrates through Abu Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb regarding [Quran 24:40](quran://24/40): *"He moves about in five kinds of darkness: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entering is darkness, his emerging is darkness, and his ultimate destiny on the Day of Resurrection is to the darkness of the Fire (`fa-huwa yataqallabu fī khamsin min al-ẓulam: kalāmuhu ẓulmah, wa-ʿamaluhu ẓulmah, wa-madkhaluhu ẓulmah, wa-makhrajuhu ẓulmah, wa-maṣīruhu yawma al-qiyāmati ilā al-ẓulumāt ilā al-nār`)."*
  * **Ibn ʿAbbās:** Narrated via Muhammad ibn Saʿd: *"By 'the darkness', He means the deeds; and by 'the deep sea', the heart of the human being. He said: {a wave covers him, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud}, he said: {darkness upon darkness}, by that He means the covering that is over the heart, the hearing, and the sight, and that is like His saying: {Allah has set a seal upon their hearts...} ([Quran 2:7](quran://2/7))."*
  * **Qatādah, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd:** Qatādah stated that *baḥr lujjiyy* means deep (*ʿamīq*), and it is a parable God set forth for the disbeliever acting in misguidance and confusion. Al-Suddī and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas shared identical interpretations of compounding blindness. Ibn Zayd explained `ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ` as: *"Evil, some of it upon another (`sharrun baʿḍuhu fawqa baʿḍ`)."*
* **The Classical Identification of the Three Physical Darknesses:** In [Tafsir al-Tabari 24:40](tabari://24/40), al-Ṭabarī explicitly explains the physical stacking of the two surface waves directly beneath the clouds:
  `يَقُولُ: يَغْشَى الْبَحْرَ مَوْجٌ (مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ) يَقُولُ: مِنْ فَوْقِ الْمَوْجِ مَوْجٌ آخَرُ يَغْشَاهُ، (مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ) يَقُولُ: مِنْ فَوْقِ الْمَوْجِ الثَّانِي الَّذِي يَغْشَى الْمَوْجَ الْأَوَّلَ سَحَابٌ`
  (*"He says: A wave covers the sea; {above which is a wave} He says: above the wave is another wave covering it; {above which is a cloud} He says: above the second wave which covers the first wave is a cloud."*)
  Subsequent classical commentators—including al-Baghawī in *Maʿālim al-Tanzīl*, al-Qurṭubī in *al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān*, and al-Maḥallī in *Tafsīr al-Jalālayn*—summarized these three macroscopic physical barriers to light in the concise formula:
  `ظُلْمَةُ الْبَحْرِ وَظُلْمَةُ الْمَوْجِ وَظُلْمَةُ السَّحَابِ`
  (*"the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the waves, and the darkness of the clouds"*):
  1. *Ẓulmat al-baḥr* (the darkness of the deep water),
  2. *Ẓulmat al-mawj* (the darkness of the cresting waves),
  3. *Ẓulmat al-saḥāb* (the darkness of the rain clouds overhead), augmented by *ẓulmat al-layl* (the darkness of night).
  Neither al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr, nor any early commentator ever conceived of these waves as separated by hundreds of meters of depth; they are the successive waves of a tempest tossed by wind beneath dark storm clouds.
* **Classical Exegetical Evaluation of 'He Can Hardly See It' (*Lam Yakad Yarāhā*):** Al-Ṭabarī analyzes the three recognized grammatical interpretations of `إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا` (*idhā akhraja yadahu lam yakad yarāhā*):
  1. *Complete Negation:* He does not see it at all (*lam yarāhā*), where *kāda* serves to emphasize the sheer impossibility of sight due to intense darkness (as held by al-Zajjāj, Abu ʿUbaydah, and al-Farrāʾ).
  2. *Negation of Proximity:* He does not even come close to seeing it (*lam yaqrab an yarāhā*). As the grammarian Radī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī noted in his commentary on *al-Kāfiyah* (2:306): *"Negating the proximity of an action is more emphatic in negating that action than negating the action itself."*
  3. *Vision with Extreme Effort:* He sees it only after prolonged effort and despair (*baʿda buṭʾin wa-jahd*), reflecting standard Arabic parlance (*mā kidtu arāka*). Al-Ṭabarī clarifies that this figurative expression is aesthetically fitting because it is a literary parable (*mathal*), not an empirical scientific report about a physical object (*wa-innamā ḥasuna dhālika fī hādhā al-mawḍiʿ... li-anna dhālika mathalun lā khabarun ʿan kāʾinin kān*).
